signals.title: Compactor delete-request-store initialization fails independently of the main S3 object-store client
signals.text: ## Problem In Loki 3.6.11, the main object-store path and the compactor delete-request-store path are initialized separately. In my production setup with an Amazon S3 Express One Zone directory bucket, the main storage client can operate, but the compactor can still fail during delete-request-store initialization when retention is enabled. The failure I see is: ```text failed to init delete store: Get "https://<bucket>.s3express-<zone>.<region>.amazonaws.com/?session=": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ``` ## The two client-creation paths ### 1) Main object/data/index client Loki creates the main object clients here: - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1670-1681` builds the per-period object clients with `storage.NewObjectClient(periodConfig.ObjectType, "compactor", ...)` - `pkg/storage/factory.go:658-709` routes S3 backends to `aws.NewS3ObjectClient(...)` - `pkg/storage/chunk/client/aws/s3_storage_client.go:176-255` builds the AWS S3 client and applies `http_config.ca_file` to the HTTP transport ### 2) Compactor delete-request-store client The delete-store client is created separately here: - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1684-1690` builds `storage.NewObjectClient(deleteStore, "delete-store", ...)` - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1696-1700` passes that client into the compactor - `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:212-219` immediately initializes delete handling when `retention_enabled` is true - `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:315-336` wires the delete-request store into the deletion manager ## Why this matters The compactor startup path touches the delete-request-store immediately when retention is enabled, so any TLS / trust-store mismatch on that path prevents the backend from starting even though the main object-store path is a separate client and may otherwise behave differently at runtime. In practice this is painful for S3 Express because the failure happens during the `CreateSession`/session bootstrap path for the directory bucket, and the pod can look like it is failing only at startup rather than during ordinary reads/writes. ## Expected behavior The delete-request-store client should inherit the same S3 TLS trust configuration as the main object-store client, or Loki should expose a clear, documented way to configure the CA bundle for that path as well. ## Suggested fix Please review whether the delete-request-store initialization path is missing parity with the main object-store path for custom TLS trust / CA bundle handling, especially for S3 Express directory buckets.
signals.author: vbichov

signals.title: [Helm] extraObjects: tpl re-evaluates user content, breaking Prometheus/Loki ruler templates ({{ $labels }}, {{ $value }})
signals.text: **Describe the bug** The Loki Helm chart's `extraObjects` field passes every user-provided entry through `tpl`, which re-evaluates the rendered YAML as a Helm template. Any embedded `{{ ... }}` that targets a *different* runtime (Prometheus/Loki ruler alert templates such as `{{ $labels.x }}` / `{{ $value }}`, Grafana templating, etc.) is therefore evaluated by Helm at chart-render time and fails with `undefined variable`. Concrete impact: shipping Loki ruler alert rules as a ConfigMap via `extraObjects` is impossible without manually backtick-escaping every `{{ $labels.* }}` and `{{ $value }}` in every rule. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Use Loki Helm chart `grafana/loki` (reproduced on 6.6.0; the relevant template is identical on current `main` / 7.1.0). 2. Create `values.yaml`: ```yaml extraObjects: - apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: loki-alert-rules data: rules.yaml: | groups: - name: example rules: - alert: TestAlert expr: rate({job="x"} |= "error" [5m]) > 0 annotations: summary: "Error spike on {{ $labels.cluster }}" ``` 3. Render the chart: ```bash helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.6.0 -f values.yaml ``` No Loki / Alloy instance is needed — this fails at chart render time. **Expected behavior** `helm template` renders the ConfigMap with `{{ $labels.cluster }}` preserved as a literal string, so the Loki ruler can substitute it at alert evaluation time. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (any; bug is at `helm template` time) - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.6.0; same code in `main`) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Render error: ``` Error: template: loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml:N:M: executing "loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml" at <tpl (toYaml .) $>: error calling tpl: ... at <$labels.cluster>: undefined variable "$labels" ``` Relevant template — `production/helm/loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml`: ```yaml {{- range $extraObjects }} --- {{- if kindIs "map" . }} {{- tpl (toYaml .) $ | nindent 0 }} # re-evaluates user content {{- else if kindIs "string" . }} {{- tpl . $ | nindent 0 }} {{- end }} {{- end }} ``` --- **Root cause** `tpl` is applied to every `extraObjects` entry so users can interpolate Helm context (e.g. `{{ .Release.Name }}`) inside their manifests. The same call also eagerly evaluates any other `{{ ... }}` it encounters, including expressions meant for a downstream runtime. Loki ruler templating is the most common collision because the ruler ConfigMap pattern is widely used. **Current workaround** Backtick-escape each `{{ ... }}` so Helm emits a literal: ```yaml summary: "Error spike on {{ `{{ $labels.cluster }}` }}" ``` Works but is intrusive — a rule with 3 annotations needs 3 escapes each, and every new rule needs the same treatment. Copy-pasting rules from an existing Prometheus deployment doesn't just work. **Proposed fix** Add an additive, non-breaking values key `extraObjectsNoTpl` that mirrors `extraObjects` but skips `tpl`: ```yaml # values.yaml # Extra Kubernetes manifests appended to the release, NOT processed through # `tpl`. Use this for content containing expressions that must reach the # runtime as-is — e.g. Prometheus / Loki ruler alert templates # ({{ $labels.x }}, {{ $value }}). For content that needs Helm variable # interpolation, use `extraObjects` instead. extraObjectsNoTpl: [] ``` ```yaml # templates/extra-manifests.yaml — additional block {{- range .Values.extraObjectsNoTpl }} --- {{- if kindIs "map" . }} {{- toYaml . | nindent 0 }} {{- else if kindIs "string" . }} {{- . | nindent 0 }} {{- end }} {{- end }} ``` API rule: "tpl needed → `extraObjects`; raw → `extraObjectsNoTpl`". Existing `extraObjects` behavior unchanged. **Offer to send PR** Happy to open a PR implementing `extraObjectsNoTpl` (template + `values.yaml` + `values.schema.json` + `ci/` test + README) if maintainers are open to this shape. If a different API is preferred (per-entry flag, opt-out on `extraObjects`, etc.), please advise before I cut the PR. **Related** #11796 — different `extraObjects` rendering issue (uses `include`). This report specifically covers the runtime-template-variable collision via `tpl`.

signals.title: \u0022 unicode escaping in log messages on .NET 10
signals.text: **Describe the bug** When using `Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki` v9 with the default formatter on .NET 10, double quotes in log messages are escaped as `\u0022` in Grafana Loki instead of rendering as literal `"` characters. **To Reproduce** 1. Create an ASP.NET Core project on .NET 10 2. Add `Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki` v9 and configure with default formatter 3. Enable `UseSerilogRequestLogging` 4. Deploy to Azure App Service and check logs in Grafana Loki **Expected behavior** The logs should show without \u0022. For e.g. HTTP GET /Home/Dispatches responded 200 in 132.39 ms **Environment:** - Runtime: .NET 10 - Package: Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki 9.0.0 - Infrastructure: Azure App Service - Hosting: ASP.NET Core MVC **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Screenshot attached. **Workaround** Use `RenderedCompactJsonFormatter` from `Serilog.Formatting.Compact` as the `textFormatter` parameter on the Loki sink: ```csharp using Serilog.Formatting.Compact; cfg.WriteTo.GrafanaLoki( uri, credentials: credentials, labels: labels, propertiesAsLabels: ["level"], textFormatter: new RenderedCompactJsonFormatter()); ```
signals.author: vssaini

signals.title: LogQL: Pretty printing json/logfmt logs
signals.text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Structured logs such as JSON or Logfmt, prevalent in most applications these days, make logs easy to query, at the expense of being difficult for humans to read. Here is one example log coming from Grafana: ``` logger=tsdb.loki endpoint=queryData pluginId=loki dsName=Loki dsUID=myuniquelokiuid uname=grafana_scheduler rule_uid=bfp7zv89ut4w0a org_id=1 fromAlert=true t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.910720711Z level=info msg="Response parsed from loki" duration=100.617µs framesLength=0 stage=parseResponse logger=ngalert.scheduler rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 version=1 fingerprint=22182789d24d049b now=2026-06-23T06:08:00Z rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.912792957Z attempt=2 max_attempts=3 next_attempt_in=1.643128315s error="the result-set has errors that can be retried: [sse.dataQueryError] failed to execute query [query]: bad_data: invalid parameter "query": 8:3: parse error: unexpected character: '|'" ``` * ❌ Human readable **msg** lost in the middle of other machine-data such as **rule_uid** and **fingerprint** * ❌ **level** lost in the middle of other machine-data * ❌ **logger** of different length misaligns the log and make it difficult to read * ❌ Noise from duplicate information such as **t**. Another example from a Python application ``` timestamp="2026-06-22 13:57:54" logger="statemonitor" level="ERROR" message="Main crashed. Goes into sleep backoff for 30 sec" thread="MainThread" user=12345, endpoint="/bar" traceback="
 File "<python-input-19>", line 4, in <module>
 lumberjack()
 ~~~~~~~~~~^^
 File "<python-input-8>", line 7, in lumberjack
 bright_side_of_life()
 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
 File "<python-input-8>", line 11, in bright_side_of_life
 return t[5]
 ~^^^
IndexError: tuple index out of range" ``` * ❌ Newlines escaped with `
` make traceback impossible to read * ❌ Attempts to restore the newlines with LogQL (`| logfmt | line_format "{{.message}} {{.traceback}}`") easily looses other KV-pairs, eg `endpoint` and `user` in the example above **Describe the solution you'd like** Helper functions in LogQL to pretty print a logfmt-formatted log, so the output after query looks as follows: ``` info tsdb.loki : Response parsed from loki. endpoint=queryData pluginId=loki dsName=Loki dsUID=myuniquelokiuid uname=grafana_scheduler rule_uid=bfp7zv89ut4w0a org_id=1 fromAlert=true duration=100.617µs framesLength=0 stage=parseResponse error ngalert.scheduler: Failed to evaluate rule. error="the result-set has errors that can be retried: [sse.dataQueryError] failed to execute query [query]: bad_data: invalid parameter "query": 8:3: parse error: unexpected character: '|'" rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 version=1 fingerprint=22182789d24d049b now=2026-06-23T06:08:00Z rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.912792957Z attempt=2 max_attempts=3 next_attempt_in=1.643128315s ERROR statemonitor : Main crashed. Goes into sleep backoff for 30 sec traceback=File "<python-input-19>", line 4, in <module> lumberjack() ~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "<python-input-8>", line 7, in lumberjack bright_side_of_life() ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "<python-input-8>", line 11, in bright_side_of_life return t[5] ~^^^ IndexError: tuple index out of range thread="MainThread" user=12345, endpoint="/bar" INFO auth : Another log entry bla bla ``` * ✅ Emphasising the most relevant fields first (`message`, `logger`, `level`, `ts`) * ✅ Aligning fields that we know will always be short and first (`level` and `logger`) * ✅ Display newlines, indented to not be mixed up with other logs. * ✅ Word wrap * ✅ Present all remaining KV-pairs after the message * ✅ Truncation Suggested LogQL might look something like this: ``` | logfmt | drop ts | pretty_print (level:align, logger:align, message, error:with_key, *rest:with_key:with_newlines) ``` I have not thought in detail about the exact semantics and am happy to leave that to the experts. Things that would be of interest to control: * Alignment * Escaping newlines or not * Displaying key name or not * Handling of missing fields, silently ignoring them or showing that they are missing Defaults for good handling of `level` `lvl`, `logger`, `msg`, `message`, `ts`, `t`, `timestamp` would also be appreciated. As i believe 99% of all logs will centre around those fields. **Describe alternatives you've considered** * Concotion of `line_format` `slice`, `align_left`, `indent`, `printf` etc. - While this works okish for the left alignment. Printing "the rest" of the KV-fields becomes difficult. ` | line_format "{{(slice .builtin_levelname 0 1)}}/{{printf "%-25s" .builtin_name}} {{printf "%-10s" .msg | indent 3}} {{ range $k, $v := . }}{{ if (eq (slice $k 0 3) "ht_" ) }}{{ slice $k 3 }}={{ $v }} {{ end }}{{ end }}"` ❌ Extremely unmaintainable and ugly * Using Grafana table view exclusively to view logs ❌ Requires a lot of clicking to select the relevant fields. ❌ Selection can not be reused and shared. ❌ Only works in Grafana, not with LogCLI or when presenting the logs through other interfaces using the Loki REST API. * Change the application to print the logs in the desired order and with labels truncated to be aligned without tooling (`warning` ->`warn`) InfluxDB has such logs for example ``` ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.766046Z lvl=info msg="Welcome to InfluxDB" log_id=13WAOWTG000 version=v2.4.0 commit=de247bab08 build_date=2022-08-18T19:41:15Z log_level=info ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.766081Z lvl=warn msg="nats-port argument is deprecated and unused" log_id=13WAOWTG000 ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.779555Z lvl=info msg="Resources opened" log_id=13WAOWTG000 service=bolt path=/var/lib/influxdb2/influxd.bolt ``` ✅ `msg` and `lvl` aligned and looks good out of the box ❌ Requires control of every application in the wild ❌ Will not work if `logger` is misaligning ❌ No story for how to deal with newlines **Additional context** https://brandur.org/logfmt#human does acknowledge that logfmt is not readable enough for humans and suggest that the presentation layer should provide additional help: > *Logfmt may be more readable than something like JSON, but it’s still difficult to scan quickly for humans.* > *In development, a log output formatter can then give the msg field special treatment by displaying it in way that a human can easily read (along with other special fields like level)*

signals.title: feat(operator): add k8s.audit.event.verb as default stream label for audit tenant
signals.text: ## What this is / why we need it The OpenShift Logging OTLP data model ([docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.5/html/configuring_logging/opentelemetry-data-model)) already maps several audit event fields to structured metadata: - `k8s.user.username` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.resource` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.namespace` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.name` - `k8s.audit.event.response.code` - `k8s.audit.event.user_agent` However, `verb` (the API operation: create, update, patch, delete, get, list) is **not included** in the default attribute mapping — neither as a stream label nor as structured metadata. `verb` is arguably the most important filter for audit log queries and is an ideal stream label candidate because: - **Very low cardinality**: only ~6 values (create, update, patch, delete, get, list) - **Static/long-lived**: values never change - **Most commonly used filter**: nearly every audit query filters by verb first - **Partitions search space effectively**: most audit volume is `get`/`list`, so filtering to `create`/`delete` dramatically reduces scan ## Proposal Add `k8s.audit.event.verb` as a **default stream label** for the `audit` tenant in `openshift-logging` mode. Since cardinality is ≤6, it creates at most 6 additional streams per existing stream combination — well within safe limits. Alternatively, at minimum add it as **structured metadata** so it can be used in label filter expressions without `| json` parsing. ## Context We're building an OCP audit log viewer dashboard ([PR](https://github.com/rhobs/observability-operator/pull/1134)) that filters by verb, username, resource, namespace, etc. Currently the query requires `| json` to parse every log line before filtering — making `verb` a stream label would allow the stream selector to eliminate most logs before parsing. ## References - [OpenShift Logging 6.5 OTLP data model](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.5/html/configuring_logging/opentelemetry-data-model) - [Label best practices](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/next/get-started/labels/bp-labels/) - Related: https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/21001 (stream label defaults discussion)
signals.author: sradco

signals.title: Loki query performance is slow
signals.text: Hi Team, facing query performance issues with Loki. We have approximately 10-30Mil data for last 24h query and it's taking around 15-20 seconds. Azure storage is our backend Please check and help to fix the performance issue. Below is our config: 6 ingesters(10gb, 2cpu), 12 queriere(4b, 2cpu) limits_config: retention_period: 336h # 14 days for QA — cheaper storage ingestion_rate_mb: 50 ingestion_burst_size_mb: 100 max_query_parallelism: 128 # Tried 32, 48 ## Adding for performance fix query_timeout: 300s max_query_length: 73h max_query_series: 2000 max_entries_limit_per_query: 50000 split_queries_by_interval: 1h # ried 30m, 2h max_streams_per_user: 0 # already set — unlimited, confirm it's applying max_global_streams_per_user: 0 # ADD THIS — controls the ingester-level global #Adding to improve ingester performance ingester_client: pool_config: client_cleanup_period: 15s #health_check_ingesters: true grpc_client_config: max_recv_msg_size: 104857600 # 100 MiB max_send_msg_size: 104857600 # 100 MiB ## Adding for performance fix frontend: max_outstanding_per_tenant: 512 query_scheduler: max_outstanding_requests_per_tenant: 512 querier: max_concurrent: 16 # Tried16, 8, 6, 4 query_ingesters_within: 1h15m # Tried 45m ,3h

signals.title: Logs disapear from querier every 3 days but re-appears when recreating the containers
signals.text: **Describe the bug** 1 in every 3 days, logs are missing from the query interface. They are sent to the object store, they are indexed, but they disappear from the interface. During the day of the logs disppearing, we could see it getting removed right after the compactor activation. The logs are missing from 0:00 UTC to 23:59:59 UTC. Logs are stored in S3 compatible storage (OVHcloud Object Storage). Logs are shipped with Alloy. All logs are affected. I tried with monolithic deploy, micro-service (read, write, backend) mode with and without shared volumes. I tried multiple configurations. The logs always appears to be removed after compactor. If I delete the volumes, and recreate the containers, the data reappears until the compactor runs again. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Started Loki v3.7.3 (also happening on 3.7.2 and 3.7.1) 2. Started Alloy (send some logs, it appears on high or low throughput) 3. Wait for a few days 4. 1 in every 3 day is missing. **Expected behavior** The logs are not missing from the query, volume or index. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Docker in a VM - Deployment tool: Ansible, with Docker. S3 compatible object storage, with versioning enabled. **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Config: ``` auth_enabled: false server: http_listen_address: 0.0.0.0 http_listen_port: 3100 grpc_listen_port: 9096 log_level: debug grpc_server_max_concurrent_streams: 1000 memberlist: join_members: - signals.title: loki-canary tls question
signals.text: Hello, I have installed loki using the latest helm chart loki from grafana official repository: https://grafana.github.io/helm-charts. In my setup I need loki-gataway to be TLS-enabled (self-signed certificate, which is fine for me), but TLS creates strange issues with loki-canary. 1. If I am just enabling tls, it cannot verify certificate ``` extraArgs: - -tls=true - -addr=loki-gateway:8443 ``` failed to connect to wss://loki-gateway:8443/loki/api/v1/tail?query=... with err tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority 2. If I am adding -insecure, it complains on absence of TLS cert/key/ca files, which is strange as it looks like it activates mTLS... ``` extraArgs: - -tls=true - -addr=loki-gateway:8443 - -insecure ``` Unable to create writer for Loki, check config: failed to create TLS config for transport: unable to read CA cert: unable to read file : open : no such file or directory 3. If I mount secret with some random key/cert/ca files it complains: "TLS configuration error: unable to use specified CA cert file /etc/tls/ca.crt" - so probably '-insecure' or '-tls' somehow activates mTLS mode which I do not need, I need just simple encryption (https). ``` extraArgs: - -tls=true - -addr=loki-gateway:8443 - -insecure - -ca-file=/etc/tls/ca.crt - -cert-file=/etc/tls/tls.crt - -key-file=/etc/tls/tls.key ``` 4. Finally if I want to disable loki-canary in the helm chart values, helm update fails: ``` Upgrade failed: execution error at (loki/templates/validate.yaml:6:4): Helm test requires the Loki Canary to be enabled ``` So the question is, how to use loki with simple TLS? Am I missing something? Thanks!

signals.title: Azure backend config does not support http_config
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** The current support for Azure environments do not include sovereign clouds. These cloud environments are indeed Azure, but they are usually airgapped or proxied and have a private set of CAs. To ensure the azure sdk inside loki connects, you can set `endpoint_suffix` to the proper Azure blob endpoint, but the TLS is still untrusted. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Install Loki (any mode up to v3.7) with a forward proxy in between Azure and loki 2. Use something like managed workload identity or hard coded keys to connect to azure's container store 3. Get untrusted CA **Expected behavior** Connects no problem **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes - Deployment tool: helm I think this could be remedied with exposing the `http_config` on the `azure` storage object much like it is on the `s3` object in the config

signals.title: Logcli: structured metadata is missing when using --tail after first batch of messages are shown
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** When querying log messages using logcli using `--tail` the `labels` section printed contains all the proper labels as well as all structured metadata fields folded into it. However every message that is printed after those initial messages are shown, only contain the proper labels and no structured metadata fields. This does happen with `--output=default` as well with `--output=jsonl`. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Started Loki (version 3.7.2) 2. Ingest logs which contain structured metadata fields. 3. Query the logs using `logcli query {xxx} --tail` **Expected behavior** Structured metadata fields being available for all messages. **Environment:** - Loki and logcli installed using the latest Debian packages available on https://packages.grafana.com/oss/deb onto Debian Trixie. - Loki is running in monolithic mode using filesystem storage. **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** The example below is coming from a production machine but i have redacted some of the metadata fields. `instance`, `job` and `service_name` are proper labels all other fields are structured metadata. The first message seen here was the last of the initial batch of messages that is printed when logcli was started. The second message was printed a couple of seconds later. ``` $ logcli query '{job="fluent-bit/systemd", service_name="ssh"}' --output jsonl --tail | jq . .... { "labels": { "CMDLINE": "\"sshd-session: [accepted]\"", "COMM": "sshd-session", "EXE": "/usr/lib/openssh/sshd-session", "GID": "0", "RUNTIME_SCOPE": "system", "SYSTEMD_CGROUP": "/system.slice/ssh.service", "SYSTEMD_SLICE": "system.slice", "SYSTEMD_UNIT": "ssh.service", "UID": "0", "instance": "prod03", "job": "fluent-bit/systemd", "level": "info", "service_name": "ssh" }, "line": "Connection closed by 192.0.2.1 port 35848 [preauth]", "timestamp": "2026-07-03T00:04:58.713467+02:00" } { "labels": { "instance": "prod01", "job": "fluent-bit/systemd", "service_name": "ssh" }, "line": "Connection closed by 192.0.2.1 port 57000 [preauth]", "timestamp": "2026-07-03T00:05:09.392838+02:00" } .... ```

signals.title: Bloom builder fails Azure uploads with "token is expired" (federated/workload identity), while chunk & compactor clients on the same identity refresh fine
signals.text: **Describe the bug** With Azure Workload Identity (`use_federated_token: true`), the **bloom-builder** fails all object-storage uploads with `InvalidAuthenticationInfo` / "Lifetime validation failed. The token is expired." once a pod is past ~1h of life. On the **same** service account, the ingester/write path (chunk flushes, incl. pods up 60+ days) and the compactor upload fine — so the federated identity itself is healthy and rotating. The bloom store uses the same client as everyone else (`NewBloomStore` → `storage.NewObjectClient(..., "bloomshipper", ...)` → `BlobStorage` with `SetCustomRefreshFunc`), and that federated-token refresh code is identical from v3.5.7 through v3.7.3 — yet only the builder fails to refresh. It looks like the deprecated `go-autorest/adal` SPT doesn't refresh reliably for the builder's infrequent/bursty access pattern (build cycles every `planning_interval`, long single tasks spanning the ~1h token lifetime). Impact: uploads never succeed → planner re-plans the same gaps every cycle → builder rebuilds blocks locally each time → the bloom shipper working dir grows unbounded and fills the backend PVC (`blocks_cache` limits don't bound builder scratch). Does [#21987 (Replace deprecated Azure SDK)](https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/21987) — moving to `WorkloadIdentityCredential`, on `main`, not yet in v3.7.3 — fix this, and which release will ship it? **To Reproduce** 1. Start Loki v3.5.7, SimpleScalable, on AKS with Azure Workload Identity: `storage.type: azure`, `use_federated_token: true`. 2. Enable blooms: `bloom_build.enabled: true`, `bloom_gateway.enabled: true`, `bloom_creation_enabled: true`, `bloom_gateway_enable_filtering: true`. 3. Let a backend pod run past ~1h and a bloom build cycle execute. 4. Watch `component=bloom-builder` logs. **Expected behavior** The bloom-builder refreshes its Azure access token (re-reading the rotated federated token file) and uploads succeed — as the chunk and compactor clients do on the same identity. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (AKS), Azure Blob storage, Azure Workload Identity - Deployment tool: helm (`loki` chart 6.42.0), SimpleScalable **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** ``` level=error caller=builder.go:519 component=bloom-builder tenant=<tenant> table=index_<N> meta=bloom/index_<N>/<tenant>/metas/<...>.json msg="failed to write meta" err="... ServiceCode=InvalidAuthenticationInfo ... AuthenticationErrorDetail: Lifetime validation failed. The token is expired. PUT https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/bloom/index_<N>/<tenant>/metas/<...>.json User-Agent: [Azure-Storage/0.14 (go1.24.8; linux)] RESPONSE Status: 401" ```
signals.author: mbailess

signals.title: pattern tee: nil-pointer panic in distributor - TenantConfigs nil because PatternIngesterTee lacks TenantConfigs module dependency
signals.text: ## Describe the bug Distributors intermittently panic (SIGSEGV) in the pattern-ingester tee path. The panic is a nil dereference of `*runtime.TenantConfigs` inside `TeeService`. It is non-deterministic per pod: some distributor pods start, serve traffic, then crash once with `exit=2`, and usually recover on restart. ## Environment - Loki: **3.5.2** (also verified in source: v3.5.3, v3.5.5, `main`) - Mode: distributed / microservices (separate `distributor` target) - `auth_enabled: false` (single tenant `fake`) - `pattern_ingester.enabled: true` - `runtime_config` effectively empty (`{}`) ## Stack trace ``` panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x299258c] runtime.(*TenantConfigs).getOverridesForUser(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:80 runtime.(*TenantConfigs).LogPushRequestStreams(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:98 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch.func1(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:347 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:299 pattern.(*TeeService).batchSender(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:279 pattern.(*TeeService).Start.func1() pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:120 created by pattern.(*TeeService).Start pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:119 ``` ## Root cause (analysis) - `getOverridesForUser` (pkg/runtime/config.go) panics because the receiver `*TenantConfigs` (`ts.tenantCfgs`) is `nil`, not because the provider is nil. - `initPatternIngesterTee` builds the tee with `t.tenantConfigs` (pkg/loki/modules.go), but the module dependency graph does **not** list `TenantConfigs` as a dependency of `PatternIngesterTee`: ``` PatternIngesterTee: {Server, Overrides, MemberlistKV, Analytics, PatternRingClient} ``` So depending on module init order, `t.tenantConfigs` can still be `nil` when the tee is constructed. The tee stores it as-is and later dereferences it in the async `batchSender` goroutine (`tee_service.go`), with no nil guard. - This is distinct from the already-merged fixes #14665 (added `Overrides` dep, 3.3.0) and #16112 (initialize overrides for pattern tee, 3.5.0): those address the `Overrides` object, not `TenantConfigs`. - Verified the gap persists in v3.5.2, v3.5.3, v3.5.5 and `main`: `PatternIngesterTee` still omits `TenantConfigs`, and `NewTeeService` / `sendBatch` still dereference `tenantCfgs` without a nil check. ## Impact - Distributor process crash -> transient 5xx on in-flight pushes (clients retry to other distributors; effective log loss ~0), pod churn, HPA jitter. - Only the patterns write path is affected; normal ingest and queries are fine. ## Suggested fix Either (or both): 1. Add `TenantConfigs` to the `PatternIngesterTee` dependencies in `setupModuleManager` so `t.tenantConfigs` is initialized before the tee is built. 2. Add a nil guard in `TeeService` before calling `ts.tenantCfgs.LogPushRequestStreams(...)`. ## Workaround Set `pattern_ingester.enabled: false` (the tee is gated by `if !Pattern.Enabled`), which removes the tee and the panic.
signals.author: capsuleci

signals.title: approx_topk() fails with parse error when using operator's custom LogQL parser
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** In the Loki Operator, when using `approx_topk()` with a custom LogQL parser setup (Observatorium API gateway), queries fail with a syntax error. The error originates from the query-frontend pod, not from the custom gateway/parser. Other newly added LogQL functions (like `variants()`) work correctly through the same setup, and `approx_topk()` works in standalone Loki installations. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Provision kubernetes or OpenShift cluster 2. Deploy Loki Operator with: - custom operator image, built from: https://github.com/btaani/loki/tree/enable_multi_variant_queries - custom Observatorium API gateway (`quay.io/btaani/api:new-logql-features-83d0dd0-multiarch`) 3. Deploy Loki components using image: `grafana/loki:3.7.3` (also tested with `grafana/loki:3.6.5` and `grafana/loki:latest`) 4. Query using logcli: ```bash export LOKI_ADDR="https://<your lokistack address>/api/logs/v1/application" export LOKI_BEARER_TOKEN="$(oc whoami -t)" export LOKI_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY="true" logcli instant-query 'approx_topk(3, bytes_over_time({kubernetes_namespace_name="<any app namespace>"}[1m]))' ``` 5. Observe error: ```bash parse error at line 1, col 1: syntax error: unexpected IDENTIFIER (<nil>) attempts remaining: 0 Query failed: run out of attempts while querying the server ``` exact error on the query-frontend pod: ```bash level=info ts=2026-07-08T12:52:51.221017611Z caller=roundtrip.go:412 org_id=application msg="executing query" type=instant query="approx_topk(3, bytes_over_time({kubernetes_namespace_name=\"log-test-0\"}[1m]))" query_hash=353573704 level=warn ts=2026-07-08T12:52:51.225403372Z caller=retry.go:125 org_id=application msg="received an error but not a retryable code, this is possibly a bug." code=Code(400) err="rpc error: code = Code(400) desc = parse error at line 1, col 1: syntax error: unexpected IDENTIFIER" ``` **Expected behavior** The approx_topk query should execute successfully and return results similar to how it works in standalone Loki installations **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (OpenShift) - Deployment tool: Operator - Loki versions tested: v3.6.5, v3.7.3, latest (all exhibit same behavior) - Query path: logcli → Observatorium API gateway (with custom parser) → query-frontend → querier - Custom parser implementation of approx_topk: https://github.com/btaani/api/tree/new-logql-features - Operator image used: https://github.com/btaani/loki/tree/enable_multi_variant_queries

signals.title: Regression (3.6.0+): compactor retention fails on boltdb-shipper chunks spanning an index-period boundary ("could not find entry of chunk ... to remove it")
signals.text: ## Summary Since **v3.6.0**, compactor retention with a `boltdb-shipper` schema fails to delete any chunk whose time range spans an index-period (table) boundary, and — because one table error aborts the whole run — this blocks retention entirely. `loki_compactor_apply_retention_last_successful_run_timestamp_seconds` stays at `0`, no marks are written, and nothing is deleted. This is a regression from **#19093** ("make index updates idempotent from horizontally scalable compactor", commit `0b2d0b070`, first released in v3.6.0). It is present in all `v3.6.x`, all `v3.7.x` (latest `v3.7.3`), and `main`. `v3.5.x` and earlier are not affected. ## Symptom Every retention cycle logs, for the table currently at the retention boundary: ``` level=error msg="failed to apply retention" table=<index_NNNNN> err="could not find entry of chunk <user>/<fp>/<from>:<through>:<checksum> to remove it" ``` `markForDelete` returns this error, the whole `RunCompaction(applyRetention=true)` aborts, `MarkPhaseFinished()` is never called, so `applyRetentionLastSuccess` is never set and the sweeper reports `no marks file found`. ## Root cause `seriesCleaner.RemoveChunk` (`pkg/storage/stores/shipper/indexshipper/boltdb/compactor/iterator.go`) recomputes a chunk's index-write entries for its full `[from, through]` via `GetChunkWriteEntries` (`pkg/storage/stores/series/index/schema.go`), which iterates **every index period the chunk overlaps**: ```go for _, bucket := range s.buckets(from, through, userID) { // one bucket per period spanned entries, _ := s.entries.GetChunkWriteEntries(bucket, ...) result = append(result, entries...) } ``` For a chunk that spans a day boundary, this yields keys for **two** day-buckets (`d<N-1>` and `d<N>`). But each per-day table only holds its own day's entries, so when processing table `index_<N>` the `d<N-1>` key is legitimately absent. `#19093` made that absence fatal: ```diff -func (s *seriesCleaner) RemoveChunk(...) error { +func (s *seriesCleaner) RemoveChunk(...) (bool, error) { indexEntries, _ := s.schema.GetChunkWriteEntries(from, through, ...) for _, indexEntry := range indexEntries { key := indexEntry.HashValue + separator + indexEntry.RangeValue - if err := s.bucket.Delete(key); err != nil { // Delete is a no-op if key absent (tolerant) - return err - } + if s.bucket.Get(key) == nil { // any absent key -> "not found" + return false, nil + } + keys = append(keys, key) } + for _, key := range keys { s.bucket.Delete(key) } - return nil + return true, nil } ``` ```diff // markForDelete, pkg/compactor/retention/retention.go -if err := indexFile.RemoveChunk(c.From, c.Through, ...); err != nil { return err } +chunkExisted, err := indexFile.RemoveChunk(c.From, c.Through, ...) +if err != nil { return err } +if !chunkExisted { + return fmt.Errorf("could not find entry of chunk %s to remove it", c.ChunkID) +} ``` Before `#19093`, `bucket.Delete` on a key that isn't in the current table was a harmless no-op, so each per-day table dropped its own entries for a spanning chunk independently and retention completed. The new "`Get` every key, fail if any is missing" logic turns the normal per-period split into a hard error. It is symmetric: processing `index_<N-1>` fails on the `d<N>` key, so both adjacent tables report `status="failure"`. Because chunks routinely stay open across midnight (see next section), the boundary table fails on essentially every retention cycle, so retention never advances. ## Chunks spanning an index-period boundary are expected by design This is not an anomaly or corrupted data — it is intrinsic to Loki's data model, which is why this regression is easy to miss but affects everyone on boltdb-shipper: - **Ingesters do not cut chunks on index-period boundaries.** Chunks are cut by age (`max_chunk_age`), size, or synchronization. `cutChunkForSynchronization` (`pkg/ingester/stream.go`) offsets each stream's sync point by its fingerprint (`(entryTimestamp + fp) % sync_period`) and only cuts above `sync_min_utilization`, so cuts are deliberately **not** wall-clock/day-aligned, and low-volume streams are not cut at all. A stream active across midnight therefore produces a chunk that spans two daily tables. - **The index model deliberately accommodates multi-period chunks.** The write path indexes a chunk in *every* period it overlaps (`GetChunkWriteEntries` → `buckets(from, through)` above), and the read path (`GetChunksForSeries`, etc.) reads across periods the same way. - **Retention itself already anticipates cross-table chunks.** `markForDelete` has a dedicated branch for `c.Through.After(tableInterval.End)` ("the chunk would also be indexed in the next table"). Both that branch and the main deletion branch now route through the strict `RemoveChunk` and hard-fail. So the correct long-term behavior is that the retention delete path must handle multi-period chunks consistently with the write/read paths (as it did before `#19093`) — the fix should not assume a chunk's entries all live in a single table. ## Reproduction 1. Configure a `boltdb-shipper` schema (`index.period: 24h`) on object storage, with compactor `retention_enabled: true`. 2. Ensure a stream stays open across a day boundary so at least one chunk spans two daily tables (normal for low-volume streams; guaranteed over time). 3. Let the retention boundary reach a day containing such a chunk. 4. On v3.6.0+: `apply_retention_last_successful_run_timestamp_seconds` stays `0`, the sweeper logs `no marks file found`, and the compactor logs `failed to apply retention … could not find entry of chunk … to remove it` on the boundary table every cycle. The same setup on v3.5.x deletes normally. ### Concrete example (schema v12) A chunk spanning `d19558` → `d19559` (open across one midnight) has these entries, one per day, in the respective tables: ``` in index_19559: fake:d19559:<seriesID>\x00<through_rel_to_d19559>\x00\x00<chunkID>\x003\x00 in index_19558: fake:d19558:<seriesID>\x00<through_rel_to_d19558>\x00\x00<chunkID>\x003\x00 ``` Both entries are present and well-formed (the index is healthy). While processing `index_19559`, `RemoveChunk` recomputes both keys and does `bucket.Get()` on each: ``` d19558 key -> nil (it lives in index_19558) => chunkExisted=false => "could not find entry of chunk" d19559 key -> found ``` ## Affected versions - Broken: **v3.6.0 → v3.7.3 (latest) and `main`** (all contain `0b2d0b070` / #19093). - Last unaffected: **v3.5.x** (`RemoveChunk(...) error`, tolerant `bucket.Delete`). - Not fixed in any release or on `main`. ## Expected behavior A chunk that spans an index-period boundary must remain removable per-table: `RemoveChunk`/`markForDelete` should only require/remove the index entries that belong to the table currently being processed (scope the recomputed entries to the table interval), and/or not treat a key that legitimately lives in an adjacent table as `chunkExisted=false`. Separately, a single table's retention error should not abort retention for all other tables. ## Not a duplicate of #20547 #20547 is the **sweep** phase timing out on marker files that already exist (`failed to process marks`). This is the **mark** phase, where no marker files are ever produced (`no marks file found`). Different phase and code path. ## Environment - Loki: reproduced on v3.7.3; regression present since v3.6.0 and on `main` - Deployment: distributed mode, object storage (S3) - Schema: `boltdb-shipper`. Only `boltdb-shipper` tables are affected; `tsdb` is not. This primarily impacts deployments still holding boltdb-shipper data within their retention window while running v3.6.0+ (i.e. mid-migration to TSDB).

signals.title: panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1] github.com/grafana/loki/v3/pkg/logproto.encodeVarintLogproto
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** Loki reports a go panic on a single (1 out of 9) read target pod. **To Reproduce** N/A **Expected behavior** A go panic should never appear **Environment:** - Infrastructure: [e.g., Kubernetes, bare-metal, laptop] - Deployment tool: helm - Loki: 3.7.2 **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** ``` panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1] goroutine 18915733 [running]: github.com/grafana/loki/v3/pkg/logproto.encodeVarintLogproto(...) /src/loki/pkg/logproto/logproto.pb.go:9028 github.com/grafana/loki/v3/pkg/logproto.(*SampleQueryRequest).MarshalToSizedBuffer(0x3a64ffdb6a80, {0x3a6504d26780, 0x24b, 0x24b}) /src/loki/pkg/logproto/logproto.pb.go:6882 +0x59e github.com/grafana/loki/v3/pkg/logproto.(*SampleQueryRequest).Marshal(0x3a64ffdb6a80) /src/loki/pkg/logproto/logproto.pb.go:6799 +0x4d google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl.legacyMarshal({{}, {0x5b686d8, 0x3a6505044b30}, {0x0, 0x0, 0x0}, 0x0}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl/legacy_message.go:408 +0xf2 google.golang.org/protobuf/proto.MarshalOptions.size({{}, 0x80?, 0x6a?, 0xdb?}, {0x5b686d8, 0x3a6505044b30}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/protobuf/proto/size.go:52 +0xfc google.golang.org/protobuf/proto.MarshalOptions.Size({{}, 0x0?, 0x2c?, 0x6f?}, {0x5aa3ae0?, 0x3a6505044b30?}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/protobuf/proto/size.go:34 +0x4c google.golang.org/protobuf/proto.Size(...) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/protobuf/proto/size.go:20 google.golang.org/grpc/encoding/proto.(*codecV2).Marshal(0x4?, {0x56f2c00?, 0x3a64ffdb6a80?}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/encoding/proto/proto.go:51 +0x7a go.opentelemetry.io/collector/pdata/internal/otelgrpc.(*codecV2).Marshal(0x0?, {0x56f2c00?, 0x3a64ffdb6a80}) /src/loki/vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/collector/pdata/internal/otelgrpc/encoding.go:61 +0x133 google.golang.org/grpc.encode({0x7efd2ea9cbb8?, 0x3a64f2d9c2b0?}, {0x56f2c00?, 0x3a64ffdb6a80?}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/rpc_util.go:804 +0x4a google.golang.org/grpc.prepareMsg({0x56f2c00?, 0x3a64ffdb6a80?}, {0x7efd2ea9cbb8?, 0x3a64f2d9c2b0?}, {0x0, 0x0}, {0x0, 0x0}, {0x5ad1528, 0x3a64f24fbce0}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/stream.go:1892 +0xe5 google.golang.org/grpc.(*clientStream).SendMsg(0x3a6522d827e0, {0x56f2c00, 0x3a64ffdb6a80}) /src/loki/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/stream.go:957 +0xf1 github.com/grafana/dskit/middleware.(*instrumentedClientStream).SendMsg(0x3a64f2f15200, {0x56f2c00?, 0x3a64ffdb6a80?}) ``` --- ## AI Summary <details> **Most likely root cause is a generated-protobuf marshal bug triggered by a mismatched size vs write path for `SampleQueryRequest`, very likely through `Plan` custom marshaling (or another nested custom field), not just a “negative value” issue.** Why I think this (high confidence): 1. Your panic is in: - `SampleQueryRequest.MarshalToSizedBuffer` (`logproto.pb.go:6882`) - then `encodeVarintLogproto` (`logproto.pb.go:9028`) 2. `MarshalToSizedBuffer` in gogo code writes backward into a pre-sized buffer. Panic `index out of range [-1]` means it wrote more bytes than were precomputed by `Size()`. 3. In `SampleQueryRequest`, the risky field is `Plan`: - it is a **customtype** (`github.com/grafana/loki/v3/pkg/querier/plan.QueryPlan`) - custom marshal/size implementations can diverge. 4. Stack goes through `proto.Size()` before marshal (grpc path), so if `Size()` underestimates by even 1 byte, reverse-write code can underflow to `-1` and panic exactly like this. So the assumption that broke is: - **“`SampleQueryRequest.Size()` exactly equals bytes written by `SampleQueryRequest.MarshalToSizedBuffer()`”** - That assumption is violated for some request shape (likely specific query plan / nested contents). --- ### What to inspect next (exactly) Open `pkg/logproto/logproto.pb.go` around lines: - `~6882` (`SampleQueryRequest.MarshalToSizedBuffer`) - `~6799` (`SampleQueryRequest.Marshal`) - `~9028` (`encodeVarintLogproto`) You want the statement at/just before line 6882 to identify which field is being encoded when it underflows. Given the struct, likely candidates in this method are: - `Plan` - `StoreChunks` - repeated `Deletes` / `Shards` - `Start`/`End` stdtime encoding But **`Plan` is the top suspect** because it is custom-typed and historically these are where Size/Marshal mismatches occur. --- ### Practical root-cause checks 1. Compare size and marshal behavior for `QueryPlan` custom type: - where its `Size()` is defined - where its `Marshal`/`MarshalTo` is defined 2. Look for non-deterministic serialization length inputs: - map iteration that affects encoded bytes - conditional fields counted differently in `Size()` vs `Marshal` 3. Check if request object is mutated after size computation and before marshal (concurrency/reuse bug). --- ### Fast mitigation - Add validation/defensive recovery before sending this RPC: - `defer recover` around call site sending `SampleQueryRequest` (temporary guard) - log the request summary (especially plan presence/shape, shards count, deletes count, storeChunks presence) - If possible, bypass/clear `Plan` for affected path to confirm hypothesis quickly. --- If you want, next I can pinpoint the exact offending field by reading those exact line ranges and tracing where `SampleQueryRequest` is constructed in Loki. </details>

signals.title: ruler.evaluation.query_frontend gRPC client message size appears configurable via flags only, not via YAML and limits to 4MiB
signals.text: **Describe the bug** Hello, I am running loki 3.7.3 and using the ruler to aggregate netflow logs to metrics. however i receive these error messages very frequently. So I asked AI to understand the issue and it seems to be a 4MB limit because the variable has different syntax or is not available in the YAML configuration and does not use the configured limit from the loki.yml. This is the AI summary: `rule evaluation failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (5054383 vs. 4194304) ` This happens on the remote evaluation path of the ruler. From the code, the relevant parts seem to be: Loki: `pkg/ruler/evaluator_remote.go` especially: ``` DialQueryFrontend() QueryFrontendConfig (*RemoteEvaluator).query() ``` dskit: ``` grpcclient/grpcclient.go especially: type Config struct RegisterFlagsWithPrefix() CallOptions() DialOption() ``` Relevant source files: https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/pkg/ruler/evaluator_remote.go https://github.com/grafana/dskit/blob/main/grpcclient/grpcclient.go QueryFrontendConfig embeds grpcclient.Config: ``` type QueryFrontendConfig struct { Address string `yaml:"address"` ClientConfig grpcclient.Config `yaml:",inline"` } ``` and registers flags via: `c.ClientConfig.RegisterFlagsWithPrefix("ruler.evaluation.query-frontend", f) ` However, in our setup, YAML fields like these are rejected: ``` ruler: evaluation: query_frontend: max_recv_msg_size: 16777216 max_send_msg_size: 16777216 grpc_compression: snappy connect_timeout: 5s ``` with errors like: ``` field max_recv_msg_size not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field max_send_msg_size not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field grpc_compression not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field connect_timeout not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig ``` At the same time, the corresponding CLI flags appear to exist: ``` -ruler.evaluation.query-frontend.grpc-max-recv-msg-size -ruler.evaluation.query-frontend.grpc-max-send-msg-size ``` So it looks like the gRPC client settings for ruler.evaluation.query_frontend are exposed via flags, but not actually accepted via YAML config. Could you please clarify whether this is expected? If not, it seems something is missing around YAML unmarshalling / inlining for QueryFrontendConfig and its embedded grpcclient.Config. It would be helpful if the same settings supported by flags were also supported in YAML for: ``` ruler.evaluation.query_frontend.max_recv_msg_size ruler.evaluation.query_frontend.max_send_msg_size ``` and related embedded grpcclient.Config fields **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start Loki 3.7.3 with monolithic mode and ruler + remote 2. ``` evaluation: mode: remote max_jitter: 0s query_frontend: address: dns:///fm1lo.sub.domain.de:9097 tls_enabled: false tls_cert_path: "" tls_key_path: "" tls_ca_path: "" tls_server_name: "" tls_insecure_skip_verify: false tls_cipher_suites: "" tls_min_version: "" ``` 3. Big queries or remote rule executions fail. **Expected behavior** A parameter to configure this limit in the yaml. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Baremetal, monolithic mode - Deployment tool: binary **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** N/A

signals.title: Automatically set GOMEMLIMIT from the cgroup memory limit at runtime (adopt automemlimit)
signals.text: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Today Loki relies on a manually configured, static GOMEMLIMIT to keep the Go runtime's memory usage under the container memory limit and avoid OOM kills. This is fragile because GOMEMLIMIT and the actual container memory limit can easily drift out of sync. Changing the container's resources.limits.memory through any path other than the Helm value (e.g. a Kustomize overlay, a manually patched manifest, VPA, or a non-Helm deployment) does not update GOMEMLIMIT. The Go runtime keeps using the stale value. The result is either OOM kills (limit lowered, GOMEMLIMIT still high) or overly aggressive GC / wasted memory (limit raised, GOMEMLIMIT still low). Components like the query-frontend are especially sensitive to this because their memory usage is bursty and GC-tunable, so a stale GOMEMLIMIT directly translates into OOMs. **Describe the solution you'd like** Have Loki set GOMEMLIMIT automatically at runtime from the cgroup memory limit, using a configurable percentage, by adopting [github.com/KimMachineGun/automemlimit](https://github.com/KimMachineGun/automemlimit). Concretely: - Initialize automemlimit early in Loki's main (cmd/loki) so it runs before the app starts. - Respect an explicit GOMEMLIMIT if the user has already set one (automemlimit is a no-op when GOMEMLIMIT is set). - Allow tuning the fraction via AUTOMEMLIMIT (e.g. default 0.9, or align with the chart's existing 0.85). **Describe alternatives you've considered** Manual static GOMEMLIMIT env var: no percentage support and must be manually kept in sync with the limit.
signals.author: zoelandeyro

signals.title: Proposal: Add native OCI Object Storage support via Thanos objstore.
signals.text: ## Problem Loki does not currently expose OCI Object Storage as a supported Thanos object-store backend. OCI users therefore have to use the S3-compatible API and static Customer Secret Keys. This prevents using OCI-native authentication mechanisms such as: - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal - Resource Principal ## Proposed solution Add `oci` to Loki's Thanos object-store backends by reusing the OCI provider from Thanos objstore. Proposed configuration: ``` storage_config: use_thanos_objstore: true object_store: oci: provider: instance-principal bucket: loki-data region: ap-tokyo-1 max_request_retries: 3 request_retry_interval: 1 schema_config: configs: - from: 2026-08-01 store: tsdb object_store: oci schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ``` ## Security benefit No OCI Customer Secret Key needs to be stored in Loki configuration or Kubernetes Secrets. ## Scope - Loki TSDB object storage - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal - Unit tests - OCI/OKE integration test documentation Named stores and Helm chart support can be submitted separately. ## Validation A standalone Thanos OCI client has already been validated successfully against OCI Object Storage from OKE using Instance Principal.

Further our local Nutanix s3 May send Errors Like http 503 "StorageFull" and s3 still Hammers the s3. signals.title: Volume API and index stats over-report after log deletion; log queries stay correct
signals.text: **Describe the bug** After the compactor processes a delete request (filter-and-delete), `/loki/api/v1/index/volume` and `/loki/api/v1/index/stats` over-report the affected streams for hours, while log/metric queries (`bytes_over_time` etc.) remain exact throughout. A second delete against the same stream selector roughly doubles the namespace's index references, inflating even query windows that are disjoint from every deleted range. The inflation survives pod restarts and does not converge within hours. This matters to anyone composing the Volume API with the delete API for per-tenant/per-namespace usage accounting: after the first delete, volume readings for that stream set can no longer be trusted. **To Reproduce** Loki 3.7.4, single binary, filesystem object store, TSDB v13 schema, `auth_enabled: false`. Compactor settings tightened only to shorten the wait: `compaction_interval: 2m`, `delete_request_cancel_period: 1m`, `retention_delete_delay: 5m`. 1. Push ~30 MB of synthetic logs (3 streams, one `namespace` label value, timestamps spread over the past 6 h), then `POST /flush`. 2. Baseline agrees: instant volume query reports 29.95 MB vs 30.18 MB ground truth from `sum(bytes_over_time(...[7h]))` (−0.8%). 3. `POST /loki/api/v1/delete` for the oldest 3 h of that namespace; wait until the request lists as `processed`. 4. `bytes_over_time` immediately reports the expected 14.84 MB (exact). The volume query for the same selector/window reports **68.1 MB**, decays stepwise (39.9 → 6.6 MB over ~10 min), then sticks at ~1.9× truth. Restarting the pod does not clear it (it read 10.6 MB after a restart). `index/stats` at that point returns **17 streams / 16,201 entries** where the actual remaining data is 3 streams / 6,946 lines. 5. Issue a second delete for part of the remaining range. After it processes, index references for the whole namespace roughly **double** (2,359 chunks / 11.16 M entries vs a clean-baseline 1,176 / 5.99 M), and a volume query restricted to a window disjoint from both deleted ranges reports ~**2.03×** its `bytes_over_time` truth, flat for 14+ minutes. A larger second dataset (3.018 GB, 6 streams) reproduced the same shape: pre-delete volume/truth ratio 1.017; after one delete a window past the deleted range stayed byte-stable; after a second delete the whole namespace's refs doubled. **Expected behavior** Volume/stats either apply delete-request filtering the way log queries do, or the docs state that these endpoints are not deletion-aware. **Root cause (from reading v3.7.4 source; code paths unchanged on `main` as of 2026-08-05)** 1. `SelectLogs`/`SelectSamples` inject pending (and recently completed) delete requests as query-time filters (`pkg/querier/querier.go`), which is why log queries stay exact through the index-cleanup transient. `IndexStats` and `Volume` in the same file take no delete parameters at all — the transient is exposed raw. 2. The querier's volume also sums the ingester's in-memory contribution (`pkg/ingester/instance.go`, unflushed chunks), which is delete-blind and WAL-durable — hence restart-proof inflation that decays as chunks flush. 3. In single-binary, the index view merges the compactor-rewritten object-store index with ingester-uploaded head TSDBs (`indexshipper` iterates the uploads manager too), which the compactor's delete processing never rewrites and which are retained for `IndexCacheValidity + 3×ResyncInterval`; the volume aggregation (`ChunkStats` summing `ChunkMeta.KB`, with pre-aggregated page markers) has no chunk-identity dedup across the merged sources, so rewritten chunks and their stale predecessors are counted together. **Environment** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (k3d), grafana-community helm chart 18.5.2 - Deployment tool: helm - Loki 3.7.4 (also inspected current `main`), single binary, filesystem object store, TSDB v13 I'm not asking for a commitment to fix — filing so the behavior is documented and searchable, since we could find no existing issue covering it. Happy to provide the full reproduction scripts.

signals.title: [loki] Document StatefulSet-immutable Helm values and upgrade/migration notes (Flux/SSA)
signals.text: ### Which chart? `loki` (official chart under `production/helm/loki`) ### What's your Loki deployment mode? All modes that render StatefulSets (Single Binary, Simple Scalable, Distributed) — especially Single Binary and Simple Scalable write/backend/ingester paths. ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Helm upgrades of the `loki` chart commonly fail with Kubernetes StatefulSet immutability errors, for example: ```text StatefulSet.apps "loki" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden ``` This is not a Flux-specific bug, but it is painful under continuous delivery (Flux `HelmRelease`, Argo CD, etc.): 1. A values change (or chart version bump) mutates a StatefulSet field outside the allowed set. 2. Helm fails to apply the upgrade (client-side or server-side apply). 3. GitOps controllers retry indefinitely → repeated HelmRelease failures and notification spam (Slack/Telegram/etc.). 4. Operators have no chart-level “immutable after install” map, so they discover the problem only at apply time. Related historical issues show this keeps recurring as chart fields evolve (closed / specific regressions): - #1154 — early chart STS field additions blocking upgrades - #9524 — `podManagementPolicy` change blocked upgrades - #19065 — chart 6.38 persistence/`accessModes` change caused STS patch failures - #12854 — PVC size changes on Single Binary STS are not live-updatable - #21675 — Single Binary `statefulset-recreate-job` path for size changes What is still missing is **durable operator-facing documentation** (and, where feasible, chart safeguards) that: - Lists which **values → StatefulSet fields** are immutable after first install - States the supported migration/recreate paths (especially `volumeClaimTemplates` / storage class / size) - Calls out GitOps/SSA implications so people can avoid flip-flopping immutable fields ### Describe the solution you'd like #### 1) Document STS-immutable value surface (primary ask) Add a short section to the Helm install/upgrade docs (and/or chart README + values comments) covering components that create StatefulSets, including at least: | Values area (examples) | STS field(s) typically affected | Mutable after install? | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `*.persistence.storageClass` / claims `storageClass` | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.storageClassName` | **No** | Requires PVC/STS migration strategy | | `*.persistence.size` / claims size | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.resources.requests.storage` | **No** (live STS patch) | Single Binary has optional recreate helper; other components need documented procedure | | `*.persistence.accessModes` | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.accessModes` | **No** | | | `*.persistence.selector` / claims selector | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.selector` | **No** | | | `*.persistence.labels` / VCT labels & name | `volumeClaimTemplates` identity | **No** | Renames/label changes on VCT block upgrades | | `*.podManagementPolicy` | `spec.podManagementPolicy` | **No** | | | `*.selectorLabels` (pod selector) | `spec.selector` | **No** | Extremely disruptive if changed | | service / headless naming that feeds `serviceName` | `spec.serviceName` | **No** | | | Most `*.persistence.annotations` (on VCT) | `volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata.annotations` | Often **No** | Depends on K8s/version; treat as risky | | Pod template: image, resources, env, probes, affinity, volumes (non-VCT), etc. | `spec.template` | **Yes** | Prefer these for day-2 changes | | `replicas`, `updateStrategy`, PVC retention policy, `minReadySeconds` | corresponding STS top-level fields | **Yes** | Per Kubernetes STS update rules | Please treat the table as a starting checklist maintainers can correct against current templates under `production/helm/loki/templates/**/statefulset*.yaml`. #### 2) Prefer template-only (mutable) knobs for day-2 ops In docs, explicitly recommend: - Prefer changes that land only in `spec.template` (config via ConfigMap/Secret hashes, resources, probes, env, extraVolumes that are not VCT-backed, etc.). - Treat storage class, PVC size, access modes, VCT labels/selectors, `podManagementPolicy`, and selector labels as **install-time** decisions unless a documented migration is followed. #### 3) Migration notes for `volumeClaimTemplates` / storage Document supported operator procedures when an immutable field *must* change, e.g.: - **PVC size increase (Single Binary):** `singleBinary.persistence.enableStatefulSetRecreationForSizeChange` and the recreate Job path — when to enable, risks, and prerequisites (storage class allowing expansion, etc.). - **storageClass / accessModes / selector changes:** safe sequence such as: 1. Ensure object storage / backup strategy is sound (filesystem single-binary vs object-storage backends). 2. Scale down or pause ingestion if required. 3. Delete StatefulSet with `cascade=orphan` (or chart-supported recreate) so PVCs are retained when intended. 4. Recreate STS with new VCT fields / re-attach or migrate data. 5. Resume traffic. - **Chart upgrades that rewrite VCT fields** (historical `#19065`-style): call out in upgrade notes when default templates change immutable fields, and whether operators must delete/recreate STS or pin values for compatibility. #### 4) GitOps / server-side apply notes (Flux, Argo, etc.) Add a short “Continuous delivery” callout: - Immutable STS field drift will fail every reconcile, not only one-shot `helm upgrade`. - Avoid oscillating values that rewrite VCT (e.g. default `null` storageClass vs explicit class) across environments. - Under server-side apply / field managers, also watch for chart-generated VCT `apiVersion`/`kind` or defaulted fields that differ from live objects and surface as forbidden updates (see past MinIO/STS defaulting issues in this chart family). - Suggested operational pattern: fail closed on immutable changes (manual approval / freeze HelmRelease) rather than retry-spam. ### Describe alternatives you've considered 1. **Rely only on Kubernetes error messages** — insufficient; does not map errors back to Helm values. 2. **Delete/recreate STS ad hoc** — works but is tribal knowledge; risky without chart-specific guidance (PVC retention, ring membership, WAL/data dirs). 3. **Use `enableStatefulSetRecreationForSizeChange` only** — currently narrow (size, Single Binary-oriented); does not cover storageClass/accessModes/selectors or all STS components. 4. **File only one-off bugs when a chart release changes an immutable field** — necessary, but does not reduce operator confusion between releases. ### Additional context **Minimal reproduce (generic):** ```bash # namespace example only — no cluster-specific names beyond monitoring/loki helm upgrade --install loki grafana/loki \ --namespace monitoring \ --create-namespace \ --set deploymentMode=SingleBinary \ --set singleBinary.replicas=1 \ --set singleBinary.persistence.enabled=true \ --set singleBinary.persistence.size=10Gi # ... storage backend values as appropriate ... # later: change an immutable-bound value helm upgrade loki grafana/loki \ --namespace monitoring \ --reuse-values \ --set singleBinary.persistence.storageClass=standard-rwo # or change accessModes / selector / podManagementPolicy / VCT labels ``` Observed: Helm reports StatefulSet update forbidden; under Flux the `HelmRelease` stays failing on each reconcile. **Why docs matter here:** the chart already exposes many STS-affecting knobs (`persistence.*`, `podManagementPolicy`, `selectorLabels`, VCT labels/annotations, claims arrays for distributed components). Operators and GitOps users need a single authoritative “do not change after install / how to migrate” page rather than discovering via failed applies. Happy to review a PR that only adds documentation; chart validation (e.g. NOTES.txt warning, or CI fixture detecting immutable field diffs) would be a welcome follow-up but is not required for this request.

signals.title: [helm] Zone-aware ingester StatefulSets emit a duplicate `name` label and become invalid when `ingester.podLabels.name` is set
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** When `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`, the three zone StatefulSet templates use the pod label `name: <prefix>ingester-zone-{a,b,c}` as the zone discriminator, and reference it from `spec.selector.matchLabels`. The same templates also append `.Values.loki.podLabels` and `.Values.ingester.podLabels` verbatim via `toYaml`, *after* their own labels and without merging. If a user sets `podLabels.name`, the rendered `spec.template.metadata.labels` therefore contains the key `name` **twice**. Two consequences: 1. The chart emits a YAML mapping with a duplicate key, which is invalid per the YAML spec regardless of what the user supplied. 2. Duplicate keys resolve last-wins, so the effective pod label becomes the user's value while `spec.selector.matchLabels` still requires the chart's. The API server rejects the StatefulSet with `` `selector` does not match template `labels` ``. The same key is also used by the per-zone headless Services (`service-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}-headless.yaml`), so a naive workaround of dropping the chart's label would leave those Services with no endpoints and break stable pod DNS. The non-zone-aware template is not affected: its selector is only `loki.ingesterSelectorLabels` and does not include `name`, so overriding `podLabels.name` there is harmless. The inconsistency looks unintentional — the zone templates added `name` to the selector without protecting it from the override path the chart itself exposes. `rollout-group` and the `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are exposed to the same collision. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0 (Loki 3.3.2). 2. Render the zone-a ingester StatefulSet with `podLabels.name` set: ```yaml # values.yaml deploymentMode: Distributed loki: storage: type: s3 bucketNames: chunks: chunks ruler: ruler admin: admin schemaConfig: configs: - from: "2024-04-01" store: tsdb object_store: s3 schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ingester: replicas: 3 podLabels: name: my-ingester # any value collides zoneAwareReplication: enabled: true read: replicas: 0 write: replicas: 0 backend: replicas: 0 ``` ``` helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.25.0 -f values.yaml \ -s templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-a.yaml ``` 3. Apply the rendered manifest to a cluster. **Expected behavior** The chart should never emit a mapping with a duplicate key, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` should always be a subset of `spec.template.metadata.labels` for any user-supplied `podLabels`. Either the chart's structurally significant labels should win over user-supplied `podLabels`, or the chart should reject the conflicting configuration with a clear message. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes 1.34 (EKS), also reproducible with `helm template` alone - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0, Loki 3.3.2) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Rendered output, `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true` — note `name` appears twice in `template.metadata.labels`, and the selector requires the first value: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a # <-- selector requires this rollout-group: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: ingester-zone-a # <-- chart's label rollout-group: ingester name: my-ingester # <-- duplicate key, wins ``` The per-zone headless Service selects on the same key: ```yaml # service-ingester-zone-a-headless.yaml selector: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a rollout-group: ingester ``` Same values with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=false` — single `name`, and the selector does not reference it, so nothing breaks: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: my-ingester ``` `kubectl apply` of the zone-aware manifest fails with: ``` The StatefulSet "loki-ingester-zone-a" is invalid: spec.template.metadata.labels: Invalid value: map[string]string{"app.kubernetes.io/component":"ingester", "app.kubernetes.io/instance":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/name":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/part-of":"memberlist", "name":"my-ingester", "rollout-group":"ingester"}: `selector` does not match template `labels` ``` --- ## Proposed fix `spec.selector` is immutable on a StatefulSet, so changing the discriminator to a dedicated key (e.g. `zone: zone-a`) would force existing zone-aware deployments to recreate their ingester StatefulSets. The options below keep the selector as it is. **Option 1 — merge the label sets so each key is emitted once (preferred).** In `templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}.yaml`, replace the `labels:` block under `spec.template.metadata` with a single merged dict, chart labels taking precedence (sprig `merge` gives precedence to the destination): ```gotemplate labels: {{- $zoneLabels := dict "app.kubernetes.io/part-of" "memberlist" "name" (printf "%singester-zone-a" (include "loki.prefixIngesterName" .)) "rollout-group" (printf "%singester" (include "loki.prefixRolloutGroup" .)) }} {{- $userLabels := merge (deepCopy (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict)) (.Values.loki.podLabels | default dict) }} {{- toYaml (merge $zoneLabels $userLabels (fromYaml (include "loki.ingesterSelectorLabels" .))) | nindent 8 }} ``` This emits every key once and guarantees `selector ⊆ labels` for any `podLabels`. Users keep the ability to add their own labels; they simply cannot silently break the selector. **Option 2 — minimal reordering.** Move the two `podLabels` blocks *above* the chart's `name` and `rollout-group` lines, so the chart's values are emitted last and win. This fixes the selector mismatch with a three-line diff, but still emits a duplicate key, so it only addresses the second consequence. **Option 3 — fail fast (complementary to either of the above).** Reject the conflicting configuration explicitly rather than rendering something that the API server will refuse: ```gotemplate {{- if and .Values.ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled (hasKey (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict) "name") }} {{- fail "ingester.podLabels may not set 'name' when ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled is true: that label is the zone discriminator used by the StatefulSet selector and the per-zone headless Services" }} {{- end }} ``` Whichever option is taken, documenting `name`, `rollout-group` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` as reserved keys under `ingester.podLabels` in `values.yaml` would help. **Workaround for anyone hitting this now** Do not set `ingester.podLabels.name` with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`. If the label is required (for example a metrics pipeline that relabels from the pod label `name`), the selector and the three per-zone headless Services have to be post-processed consistently onto a different discriminator key — all four objects must agree, or the Services lose their endpoints and stable pod DNS breaks.
