Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/23439) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib (github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pkg/pdatautil)</summary> ### [`v0.159.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v01590) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/compare/v0.158.0...v0.159.0) ##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑 - `all`: Removes the kafkatopicsobserver extension after being deprecated for 3 months ([#​48186](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48186)) Use the `kafkareceiver` with topic regex support instead. - `extension/observer`: Removes the `kafka.topics` endpoint type along with the kafkatopicsobserver extension ([#​48186](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48186)) The `observer.KafkaTopicType` endpoint type and its `observer.KafkaTopic` details struct are removed, as the kafkatopicsobserver was the only observer emitting them. The receivercreator no longer accepts `type == "kafka.topics"` rules or resource attributes for that endpoint type. - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Reserve the "*" prefix in rule names for processor-internal decision labels, and rename the unmatched-drop sentinel to `_unmatched` ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) Configs with rule names starting with "*" are now rejected at validation, so user rule names can never collide with the processor-owned sentinel labels on decision metrics (`_eviction`, `_root_span_condition`). The `rule` attribute value for traces dropped with no matching rule changes from `unmatched` to `_unmatched` to follow the same convention. - `receiver/file_log`: `ordering_criteria::top_n: 0` now means 'match all files' instead of silently behaving like `top_n: 1`. ([#​47444](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47444)) To restore the previous behavior of matching the first file only, set `ordering_criteria::top_n: 1`. ##### 🚩 Deprecations 🚩 - `exporter/azure_monitor`: Rename `azuremonitor` to `azure_monitor` ([#​45339](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45339)) - `exporter/signalfx`: Remove the logic sending trace correlation. ([#​50166](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50166)) The trace correlation endpoint is no longer processing requests as the logic has moved to be handled by the backend. With this change, the exporter continues to accept spans but will no longer send them to the correlation endpoint. - `receiver/file_log`: Deprecate the implicit `ordering_criteria.top_n` default of 1 when `ordering_criteria.sort_by` is configured. Enable the `filelog.requireExplicitTopN` feature gate to require `top_n` to be set explicitly. ([#​47444](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47444)) When `ordering_criteria.sort_by` is configured without `top_n`, the matcher silently defaults `top_n` to 1, returning only the single highest-priority file per poll. With multiple actively-written files this causes severe log duplication: the other matching files cycle in and out of the tracker and are re-read from offset 0 on rediscovery. Enabling the `filelog.requireExplicitTopN` feature gate makes an unset `top_n` a startup error when `sort_by` is configured, forcing the choice to be explicit. The gate is off by default; it is expected to become the default (and the implicit fallback removed) in a future release. Use `top_n: 1` to keep the previous behavior. Independently of the feature gate, `top_n: 0` now means "match all files" instead of silently behaving like `top_n: 1`. - `receiver/sql_query`: Rename the 'sqlquery' receiver to 'sql\_query'. The old 'sqlquery' type remains available as a deprecated alias. ([#​45339](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/45339)) ##### 🚀 New components 🚀 - `extension/sd_notify`: Introduces the `sd_notify` extension, which integrates the collector with the sd\_notify(3) protocol. ([#​49607](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49607)) ##### 💡 Enhancements 💡 - `cmd/opampsupervisor`: Add tar.gz archive support and the agent\_binary configuration for collector package upgrades. ([#​49766](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49766)) - `exporter/awscloudwatchlogs`: Add max\_event\_payload\_bytes config option to opt in to the CloudWatch Logs 1 MiB per-event limit (previously hardcoded to 256 KiB). ([#​48559](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48559)) The CloudWatch Logs PutLogEvents API began accepting events up to 1 MiB on 2025-04-02. The exporter previously truncated every event at 256 KiB (the pre-2025 service limit) via a hardcoded package constant. The default stays at 256 KiB for backwards compatibility; set `max_event_payload_bytes: 1048576` to take advantage of the new ceiling. A new `cwlogs.WithMaxEventPayloadBytes` pusher option exposes the same knob to direct callers of the internal package. - `exporter/azure_monitor`: Allow configuring HTTP status codes that should not be marked as errors in Application Insights. ([#​47691](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47691)) Adds `telemetry_mappings.traces.http.success` settings for HTTP success mapping: `additional_success_status_codes` lists status codes treated as Success on both server and client HTTP spans, and `server_policy: otel` treats 4xx responses on HTTP server spans as Success, matching the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions. Defaults preserve the existing exporter behaviour. - `exporter/load_balancing`: Promote metrics support to alpha stability ([#​50086](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50086)) - `exporter/opensearch`: Add integration test harness against a real OpenSearch instance ([#​48615](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48615)) Introduces testcontainers-go setup to validate exporter behavior, dynamic mappings, and cluster connectivity. - `exporter/prometheus_remote_write`: Add a nested `http` config block for HTTP client settings. The nested block takes precedence over flat HTTP client settings when set. ([#​46209](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46209)) - `exporter/prometheus_remote_write`: Add the exporter ID as an attribute on WAL telemetry metrics to disambiguate multiple PRW exporters sharing a collector. ([#​49130](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49130)) - `exporter/signalfx`: Stop excluding `container.memory.rss` in SignalFx exporter by default. ([#​50162](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50162)) - `extension/aws_iam_db_auth`: Change `aws_iam_db_auth` to alpha ([#​50118](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50118)) - `extension/pebble_tail_storage`: Added `max_storage_size_mib` support to the Pebble tail storage extension to bound local disk usage for pending tail-sampling trace data. ([#​49592](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49592)) Configuration example: extensions: pebble\_tail\_storage: directory: /var/lib/otelcol/pebble-tail-storage max\_storage\_size\_mib: 10240 - `extension/sumologic`: Add optional `fleet_id` configuration field to assign a collector to a fleet during registration. ([#​50142](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50142)) When fleet\_id is configured, it is sent as fleetId in the collector registration request. If the server returns an invalid\_fleet\_id or fleet\_not\_found error, registration is retried without the fleet ID so the collector can still register successfully. - `pkg/datadog`: Add the `datadog.EnableScopeConvention` feature gate to control the `otel.scope` name and version conventions in the Datadog exporter. ([#​49001](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49001)) When the `datadog.EnableScopeConvention` feature gate is enabled, spans additionally carry the `otel.scope.name` and `otel.scope.version` attributes. The deprecated `otel.library.name` and `otel.library.version` attributes are still emitted with the same values for backward compatibility, so existing dashboards and monitors keyed on them keep working. - `pkg/fileconsumer`: Move filelog.allowFileDeletion and filelog.windows.caseInsensitive filelog.featuregates to beta ([#​46635](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46635)) - `pkg/ottl`: `pcommon.Value` is now comparable using all comparison operators (==, !=, <, <=, >=, >) in OTTL expressions ([#​49170](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49170)) - `pkg/ottl`: The `set` function will pass `nil` values directly to the target when the `ottl.set.allowNil` feature gate is enabled. ([#​48714](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48714)) - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Reduce hot-path overhead with a fast path for the default root-span condition, cheaper decision-cache ordering, precomputed metric attributes, and a precomputed emitted tracestate. ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Document known limitations, the metric label contract (sentinel rule values, trigger values), and refresh the future work list ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Move buffered spans into the output at decision time instead of copying them, halving decision-path allocations. ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Drain pending traces on shutdown, deciding each through the normal rule path instead of silently dropping the buffer ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) Previously a collector restart, rollout, or config reload discarded every buffered trace without a decision (up to trace\_timeout worth of spans). Shutdown now decides each pending trace with the spans seen so far, forwards the kept ones with a correct ot=th tracestate, and reports them on the decision-triggers counter with trigger="shutdown". Traces already counted by an earlier trigger are not counted again, and the same double-count guard is applied to eviction of a trace in its decision\_delay window. - `processor/dynamic_sampling`: Use `MoveTo` instead of `CopyTo` when accumulating and forwarding spans, reducing allocations and improving throughput. ([#​49311](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49311)) - `processor/resource_detection`: Add feature gates to migrate the `elastic_beanstalk` detector to the current deployment semantic conventions. ([#​50130](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50130)) The detector reports the deployment environment as `deployment.environment`, which is deprecated in the semantic conventions, and the deployment ID as `service.instance.id`. Two alpha feature gates migrate them to `deployment.environment.name` and `deployment.id`: `processor.resourcedetection.elasticbeanstalk.EmitV1DeploymentConventions` adds the current attributes, and `processor.resourcedetection.elasticbeanstalk.DontEmitV0DeploymentConventions` removes the deprecated ones. Enabling only the first reports both sets, so telemetry can be migrated before the deprecated attributes are dropped. Enabling only the second is rejected at startup. The default output is unchanged. - `processor/resource_detection`: Support global retry config for resource detection processor ([#​46546](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46546)) - `processor/resource_detection`: Add Azure Container Apps resource detector ([#​48239](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48239)) - `processor/resource_detection`: Add the `processor.resourcedetection.consul.prefixMetaAttributes` feature gate, which emits Consul node metadata as `consul.meta.<key>` resource attributes. ([#​49988](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49988)) The gate is alpha and disabled by default, so Consul meta attribute names are unchanged unless the gate is enabled. This namespaces Consul meta consistently with the other detectors that expose user-defined key/value data, such as `ec2.tag.` and `openstack.nova.meta.`. - `processor/tail_sampling`: Add `num_shards` config option to run N parallel event loops, sharding traces by trace ID to reduce contention under high load. ([#​48699](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48699)) The single event loop can become a bottleneck under high throughput because trace ingestion starves sampling decision evaluation. Setting `num_shards` to a value greater than 1 distributes traces across independent goroutines, each with its own storage and decision batcher. The default value of 1 preserves the original single-loop behavior. To keep aggregate behavior consistent with the configured values, `num_traces`, `expected_new_traces_per_sec`, `decision_cache` sizes, and per-second rate limits in policies (`rate_limiting`, `bytes_limiting`, and composite `max_total_spans_per_second`) are divided evenly across shards. Limiter `burst_capacity` is not divided so that single large traces remain admissible regardless of the shard count. The `sampling_traces_on_memory` metric reports the total across all shards. - `processor/transform`: Add support for semconv `1.41.0`, `1.42.0` and `1.43.0` in the `set_semconv_span_name()` function. ([#​50198](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50198)) - `receiver/apache`: Change the `apache.worker.limit` metric type from a gauge to a non-monotonic cumulative sum (UpDownCounter) ([#​47061](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47061)) An UpDownCounter better represents the configured worker slots, which can go up or down over time. - `receiver/apache`: Add an opt-in migration to new, more consistent metric and attribute names behind feature gates ([#​47327](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47327)) The original metric and attribute names remain the default. Enable `receiver.apache.enableNewFormatMetrics` to also emit the new names, and additionally enable `receiver.apache.disableOldFormatMetrics` to emit only the new names. See the receiver's README for the migration guide and full mapping. Renamed metrics: - `apache.current_connections` -> `apache.connection.active` - `apache.connections.async` -> `apache.connection.status` - `apache.requests` -> `apache.request.count` - `apache.scoreboard` -> `apache.worker.status` - `apache.workers` -> replaced by `apache.worker.active` and `apache.worker.idle` Renamed attributes: - `connection_state` -> `apache.connection.state` - `state` (on the scoreboard metric) -> `apache.worker.state` - `level` (on `apache.cpu.time`) -> `apache.process.level` - `mode` (on `apache.cpu.time`) -> `cpu.mode` - `receiver/apache`: Add `apache.request.rate`, `apache.traffic.rate` (disabled by default), and `apache.worker.limit` metrics ([#​47061](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47061)) - `receiver/aws_lambda`: Add the `aws.log.subscription_filter.names` resource attribute to CloudWatch Logs decoded by the built-in decoder ([#​49923](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49923)) The subscription filter name is the CloudWatch-managed link between a log group and the destination function, so it can carry per-source identity when multiple log groups fan into a single Lambda. The attribute is only added when the event contains subscription filters. - `receiver/dns_check`: Add complete scraping implementation for the DNS Check Receiver, including metrics and resource attributes. ([#​49561](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49561)) Replaces skeleton implementation with full production-ready collector functionality. Includes metrics metadata and completed configuration. Includes real scraper implementation that performs DNS checks and emits metrics and resource attributes. Includes README docs. - `receiver/googlecloudpubsubpush`: Promote logs support to alpha stability ([#​50112](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50112)) - `receiver/kubelet_stats`: Add optional k8s node filesystem inode count/free metrics. ([#​48926](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48926)) Adds the following optional metrics to kubeletstatsreceiver: - k8s.node.filesystem.inode.count - k8s.node.filesystem.inode.free - `receiver/mysql`: Add replica thread running and open temporary table metrics to the mysqlreceiver. ([#​50132](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50132)) - `receiver/mysql`: Add mysql.file.open, mysql.table.open, and mysql.thread.slow\_launch metrics, disabled by default. ([#​49867](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49867)) - `receiver/mysql`: Add `alter_table`, `create_index`, `create_table`, and `optimize` command types to the `mysql.commands` metric. ([#​49863](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49863)) - `receiver/mysql`: Add InnoDB data I/O and pending operation metrics. ([#​50138](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50138)) - `receiver/oracledb`: Use the go-sqllexer `ObfuscateAndNormalize` engine to obfuscate SQL in the top query and query sample collectors, and upgrade `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/obfuscate` to v0.82.0 ([#​50231](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50231)) The obfuscated `db.query.text` is now normalized (whitespace collapsed, comments stripped, punctuation spaced, trailing semicolon removed), which yields stable query signatures across semantically identical statements that previously differed only in formatting. Leading SQL comments are no longer rendered as a leading `?`; the previous two-pass comment-anonymization behavior has been removed. Comment tags are still extracted from the raw SQL and emitted via `db.query.comment_tags`. Identifier quotation is preserved (`KeepIdentifierQuotation`) so a quoted identifier such as `"a b"` does not collide with the unquoted `a b`. This is a one-time change to the obfuscated output format and may alter any downstream identifiers derived from `db.query.text`. The obfuscate library upgrade to v0.82.0 (with `github.com/DataDog/go-sqllexer` v0.2.4) also normalizes qualified identifiers consistently. - `receiver/oracledb`: Add tablespace health metrics ([#​48399](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48399)) All 3 new metrics are opt-in (disabled by default) and support oracle.db.pdb on CDB-root and direct-PDB connections. Note: oracle.db.pdb is itself opt-in - if it is not also enabled on a CDB root with multiple PDBs, same-named tablespaces in different PDBs will be aggregated together rather than reported per PDB, matching the existing behavior of every other opt-in oracle.db.pdb metric in this receiver. - `receiver/oracledb`: Add wait event timeout count to the session wait sample event ([#​49934](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49934)) - `receiver/splunk_enterprise`: added dimensions to kvstore metrics ([#​50189](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50189)) - `receiver/sqlserver`: Use the go-sqllexer `ObfuscateAndNormalize` engine to obfuscate SQL in the top query and query sample collectors, and upgrade `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/obfuscate` to v0.82.0 ([#​50210](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50210)) Comment-only statements (e.g. Blue Prism banners) no longer produce a "result is empty" error or repeated error logs; they now obfuscate to an empty string. Statements the legacy tokenizer could not parse are obfuscated instead of being dropped. The obfuscated `db.query.text` is now normalized (whitespace collapsed, comments and aliases removed), which changes the obfuscated output format; this is a one-time change and may alter any downstream identifiers derived from the obfuscated query text. The obfuscate library upgrade to v0.82.0 also normalizes qualified identifiers consistently (e.g. `schema.table` no longer renders with a spurious space after the dot), which contributes to the same one-time change in obfuscated output. The transitive `github.com/DataDog/go-sqllexer` dependency is pinned to v0.2.4, which fixes obfuscation of string literals containing a backslash (e.g. `REPLACE(@​@​SERVERNAME, '\', ':')`). - `receiver/sqlserver`: Share a single, tunable database connection pool across all scrapers of a metrics or logs receiver instead of opening one pool per query. ([#​47219](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/47219)) Previously each enabled query created its own \*sql.DB connection pool to the same instance. All scrapers now share one pool per receiver instance — the metrics and logs receivers each own their own pool — that is owned by the receiver and closed on shutdown, reducing connection and memory overhead as more queries are enabled. The pool can be tuned via a new optional `connection_pool` config block (`max_open`, `max_idle`, `max_lifetime`, `max_idle_time`); by default `max_open` and `max_idle` are derived from the number of scrapers, replacing the sub-optimal Go driver defaults. Emitted telemetry is unchanged. ##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰 - `exporter/awscloudwatchlogs`: Resolve the `{PodName}` placeholder in `log_group_name`/`log_stream_name` from the `k8s.pod.name` resource attribute as well as the legacy `pod` attribute. ([#​46202](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46202)) The `k8sattributesprocessor` sets the semantic convention attribute `k8s.pod.name`, not the legacy `pod` attribute that `{PodName}` previously looked up. This left `{PodName}` resolving to `undefined` for standard EKS pipelines unless users added an extra processor to rename the attribute. - `exporter/datadog`: Fix log misrouting when a batch contains multiple ResourceLogs with different scopes, which previously routed the whole batch based on only the first ResourceLogs' scope, via the `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent` dependency bump to v0.82.0. ([#​50069](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50069), [#​49322](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49322)) - `exporter/datadog`: Fix a goroutine hang on shutdown and swallowed errors when consuming regular logs, via the `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent` dependency bump to v0.82.0. ([#​50069](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50069)) - `exporter/datadog`: Fix an unbounded loop in the histogram-to-sketch conversion that could drive the exporter to OOM when ingesting an OTel explicit-bucket histogram with a very large finite upper bound, via the `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent` dependency bump to v0.82.0. ([#​50069](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50069)) - `exporter/datadog`: Map the `Rate` metric intake type in legacy metric clients so delta-sum datapoints carrying `datadog.metric.as_type=rate` are no longer silently dropped. ([#​50119](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50119)) `toDataType` previously mapped only `Count` and `Gauge`, so a `Rate` datatype fell through to `METRICINTAKETYPE_UNSPECIFIED` and the series was rejected by the intake. - `exporter/prometheus_remote_write`: Fix context.DeadlineExceeded being incorrectly treated as a permanent error, which caused metrics to be dropped instead of retried on timeout. ([#​49691](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49691)) context.DeadlineExceeded indicates a transient timeout and should result in a retry. Only context.Canceled (explicit user/component shutdown) should be treated as permanent. - `exporter/prometheus_remote_write`: Flush buffered WAL entries when the exporter is idle so data is not stalled until the next write. ([#​49130](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49130)) - `internal/aws`: Fix `eventBatch.exceedsLimit` rolling batches at the per-event truncation cap (256 KiB) instead of the 1 MiB per-request PutLogEvents limit. Batches now pack up to the actual service ceiling. ([#​48559](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48559)) This is a pre-existing inefficiency unrelated to the new `max_event_payload_bytes` config field. `eventBatch.exceedsLimit` has compared cumulative batch bytes against `maxEventPayloadBytes` (256 KiB) rather than `maxRequestPayloadBytes` (1 MiB) since the original 2022 code. The result: batches have been rolling at \~25% of the PutLogEvents request limit. Workloads with average event size above \~25 KiB will see roughly 3-4x fewer PutLogEvents calls for the same data volume after this fix, with no config change required. The fix is also load-bearing for the new configurable per-event cap shipping in the same PR: without it, opted-in users with >256 KiB events would ship each event in its own PutLogEvents call rather than packing up to the 1 MiB service ceiling. The new threshold matches the service-documented batch-size accounting: `sum(message bytes UTF-8) + 26 * num_events`. That is exactly what `byteTotal` already sums (`eventPayloadBytes()` includes the 26-byte `perEventHeaderBytes`), so no envelope-overhead margin is needed. - `pkg/datadog`: Stop setting the removed Agent config key `enable_sketch_stream_payload_serialization`, which fixes a spurious `unknown key` ERROR logged at Agent startup. The key was a no-op, so this changes no behavior. ([#​50238](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50238)) - `pkg/translator/prometheusremotewrite`: Preserve consecutive underscores in label names when the permissive label sanitization feature gate is enabled. ([#​48991](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48991)) When the pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization feature gate was enabled, label names with consecutive underscores (e.g. a\_\_b) were still collapsed to a single underscore because the converter did not set PreserveMultipleUnderscores on the label namer. The gate now preserves them as intended. - `processor/coralogix`: Only start a new transaction for SERVER/CONSUMER spans when they cross into a different service from their parent, instead of unconditionally, so in-process phases (e.g. a queue-wait span) are no longer misclassified as separate transaction roots. ([#​50048](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50048)) Previously any SERVER or CONSUMER span nested under an existing local transaction was always split off into its own transaction root, even when it came from the same service as its parent. Root detection now compares the span's resource `service.name` against its parent's, and only treats the SERVER/CONSUMER span as a new entry point when the service actually changes. - `processor/isolationforest`: Produce differentiated anomaly scores and honor the configured `contamination_rate`. ([#​46988](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/46988)) The online isolation forest trees never split, so every record received a near-identical anomaly score and nothing was ever flagged. Trees now grow once they accumulate enough samples. The adaptive threshold also ignored `contamination_rate` (the percentile was hardcoded to 0.9); it is now derived as `1 - contamination_rate`. A `contamination_rate` of exactly 0.0 or 1.0 is now rejected during configuration validation instead of being silently replaced with a default. - `processor/k8s_attributes`: Fix memory leak and incorrect deletion for custom association identifiers (labels, annotations) that go through active->stale->active transitions. ([#​48588](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/48588)) - `processor/metrics_transform`: combine action no longer silently drops data points when a single Summary metric matches the transform. The operation is now skipped with a warning log instead. ([#​49693](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49693)) - `processor/tail_sampling`: Drop processor state when `TailStorage.Take` fails so failed fetches do not leave stranded traces or forward incomplete batches. ([#​49907](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49907)) - `processor/tail_sampling`: In the composite policy, a sub-policy omitted from `rate_allocation` now receives its default equal share of the budget instead of a zero sampling rate that permanently blocked it from sampling. ([#​49828](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49828)) - `receiver/datadog`: Set the `datadog.metric.as_type` datapoint attribute on series submitted with type `rate` ([#​50120](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50120)) A Datadog `rate` series is translated to a delta Sum, which was previously indistinguishable from one produced by a `count` series, making the original type unrecoverable downstream. Datapoints from `rate` series now carry `datadog.metric.as_type: rate`, the attribute the Datadog exporter reads to map such a Sum back to a Datadog rate. Other metric types are unchanged. - `receiver/elasticsearch`: Record deleted document counts for the index-level `elasticsearch.index.documents` metric, matching existing node-level behavior. ([#​49996](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49996)) - `receiver/icmpcheckreceiver`: Enable privileged ICMP mode on Windows so pings succeed without requiring elevated privileges. ([#​50215](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50215)) - `receiver/postgresql`: Fix EXPLAIN failing on queries with a repeated placeholder or a `$N`-looking string literal, by counting real bind parameters from `pg_prepared_statements` instead of regex-matching `$N` in the query text. ([#​50054](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50054)) - `receiver/postgresql`: Fix `postgresql.total_exec_time` and `postgresql.total_plan_time` docs on the `db.server.top_query` event to correctly state seconds instead of milliseconds. ([#​50113](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50113)) pg\_stat\_statements reports these columns in milliseconds, and the receiver correctly converts to seconds before emitting them, per OTel semantic conventions (durations SHOULD use seconds). metadata.yaml incorrectly documented the emitted unit as milliseconds; this updates the docs to match the actual (and semconv-compliant) behavior. No emitted values change. - `receiver/prometheus`: Prevent the Prometheus receiver from dropping classic histograms without explicit bucket boundaries when `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` is enabled and classic histograms are not retained. ([#​49893](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49893)) - `receiver/snowflake`: Close sql.Rows in all Fetch\* methods so the underlying driver connection is released back to the pool. ([#​49707](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49707)) Previously, none of the 8 Fetch\* methods in client.go called rows.Close() after iterating sql.Rows returned by readDB(). This leaked a database connection per query per scrape interval, eventually exhausting the connection pool. Also adds rows.Err() checks after each rows.Next() loop to surface iteration errors. - `receiver/sqlserver`: Fix query sample events silently omitting sessions blocked on schema locks. ([#​49983](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/49983)) - `receiver/sqlserver`: Fix the receiver dropping the entire query plan when obfuscating a single attribute fails ([#​50065](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50065)) All Unicode format characters (Cf category, e.g. zero-width space U+200B) are stripped from SQL before obfuscation so queries containing them are not dropped. - `receiver/yang_grpc`: Fix walking the value tree and recording metrics ([#​50109](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/50109)) <!-- previous-version --> </details> --- ### Configuration 📅 **Schedule**: (UTC) - Branch creation - At any time (no schedule defined) - Automerge - At any time (no schedule defined) 🚦 **Automerge**: Disabled by config. signal.title: feat(logql): Shard and transport approx_count_distinct sketches
signal.text: ## Summary Third slice of experimental `approx_count_distinct` ([grafana/loki-private#2769](https://github.com/grafana/loki-private/issues/2769)). Stacked on #24114. Makes the operator shardable with merge-before-estimate: queriers return raw HyperLogLog sketches, the frontend unions them by exact grouping labels, then estimates once. ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` The shard mapper rewrites that into a shared query plan. Queriers execute the sketch children; the frontend merges, then estimates: ```text CountDistinctEval< CountDistinctMerge< downstream<__count_distinct_sketch__(mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d]) by (version), shard=0> ++ downstream<__count_distinct_sketch__(mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d]) by (version), shard=1> ++ ... > > ``` Zero shards still use this merge-before-estimate shape, with a single unsharded sketch child. ## How it wires to #24114 #24114 evaluates `LabelAggregationExpr` on a single querier and returns a PromQL vector of estimates. `CountDistinctSketchExpr` existed in #24112 but still hit `EvaluatorUnsupportedType`. 1. This PR evaluates `CountDistinctSketchExpr` as a `CountDistinctVector` of HLLs (precision 14). `Merge` keys groups by the exact serialized label string, not a hash. 2. `ShardMapper` produces the plan above when `approx_count_distinct` is in `shard_aggregations`. 3. Range mapping is a no-op. Splitting numeric estimates over time would double-count overlapping values. 4. Querier results travel as `CountDistinctResponse` on the existing protobuf `QueryResponse` oneof. After merge, `Estimate()` still produces a normal PromQL vector for the public HTTP API. ## Roadmap 1. Syntax, AST, extractor (#24112) 2. Local HLL estimates on a querier (#24114) 3. **This PR** — shard + sketch eval + protobuf transport (merge-before-estimate) 4. Feature gate + result-cache bypass 5. Docs ## What to check - Review the handwritten files. Skip `pkg/logproto/sketch.pb.go` and `pkg/querier/queryrange/queryrange.pb.go`. - Merge uses exact `labels.String()`, so two groups cannot collapse. - Overlapping values across shards: `TestApproxCountDistinctShardedOverlap`. - Disabled mapping errors, and zero shards still wrap merge-before-estimate: `TestApproxCountDistinctShardMapping`. - Instant-only is still enforced before `SelectSamples`. - There is no JSON marshaler for `CountDistinctResponse`. JSON frontend encoding cannot carry sketches. ## Risks The default query-frontend still does not run this operator. `ShardMapper` requires `approx_count_distinct` in `-limits.shard_aggregations`; without it, mapping returns `approx_count_distinct is not enabled`. Direct querier `/query` from #24114 is unchanged: local estimates, no sketches on the wire. Sharded execution needs `frontend.encoding: protobuf`. That restriction is called out here and enforced in the next PR. `sum(approx_count_distinct(...))` is supposed to be correct in this PR. The inner operator is [label-reducing](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/8d8da242b61e79fb0e304f78482c392a2e538b16/pkg/logql/syntax/ast.go#L2645-L2648) and [non-additive](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/8d8da242b61e79fb0e304f78482c392a2e538b16/pkg/logql/syntax/ast.go#L2728-L2731), so the mapper [skips](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/8d8da242b61e79fb0e304f78482c392a2e538b16/pkg/logql/shardmapper.go#L270-L272) `sum(sum(x, shard=1) ++ …)` and maps the child to `CountDistinctEval` first. The outer `sum` then sees already-merged estimates. ## Test plan - [x] `go test ./pkg/logql/ ./pkg/logproto/ ./pkg/querier/queryrange/`

signal.title: feat(compaction): Merge one global ID per unique labels
signal.text: Verifies that objects about to be compacted match the expected sort order (and tenant sort-schema) of: `[ shard_bucket, tenant's sort-schema, stream fingerprint/hash, timestamp ]` If any don't match, abort the compaction run. I will handle mismatched sort-orders in a later PR. If they do match, proceed to compact them directly using k-way merge, without a CopyAndSort step at the end. It does this by calculating a new global stream table from all the inputs so matching streams will end up with the same ID and the loser-tree will correctly merge them in-order.

signal.title: [loki] Document StatefulSet-immutable Helm values and upgrade/migration notes (Flux/SSA)
signal.text: ### Which chart? `loki` (official chart under `production/helm/loki`) ### What's your Loki deployment mode? All modes that render StatefulSets (Single Binary, Simple Scalable, Distributed) — especially Single Binary and Simple Scalable write/backend/ingester paths. ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Helm upgrades of the `loki` chart commonly fail with Kubernetes StatefulSet immutability errors, for example: ```text StatefulSet.apps "loki" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden ``` This is not a Flux-specific bug, but it is painful under continuous delivery (Flux `HelmRelease`, Argo CD, etc.): 1. A values change (or chart version bump) mutates a StatefulSet field outside the allowed set. 2. Helm fails to apply the upgrade (client-side or server-side apply). 3. GitOps controllers retry indefinitely → repeated HelmRelease failures and notification spam (Slack/Telegram/etc.). 4. Operators have no chart-level “immutable after install” map, so they discover the problem only at apply time. Related historical issues show this keeps recurring as chart fields evolve (closed / specific regressions): - #1154 — early chart STS field additions blocking upgrades - #9524 — `podManagementPolicy` change blocked upgrades - #19065 — chart 6.38 persistence/`accessModes` change caused STS patch failures - #12854 — PVC size changes on Single Binary STS are not live-updatable - #21675 — Single Binary `statefulset-recreate-job` path for size changes What is still missing is **durable operator-facing documentation** (and, where feasible, chart safeguards) that: - Lists which **values → StatefulSet fields** are immutable after first install - States the supported migration/recreate paths (especially `volumeClaimTemplates` / storage class / size) - Calls out GitOps/SSA implications so people can avoid flip-flopping immutable fields ### Describe the solution you'd like #### 1) Document STS-immutable value surface (primary ask) Add a short section to the Helm install/upgrade docs (and/or chart README + values comments) covering components that create StatefulSets, including at least: | Values area (examples) | STS field(s) typically affected | Mutable after install? | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `*.persistence.storageClass` / claims `storageClass` | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.storageClassName` | **No** | Requires PVC/STS migration strategy | | `*.persistence.size` / claims size | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.resources.requests.storage` | **No** (live STS patch) | Single Binary has optional recreate helper; other components need documented procedure | | `*.persistence.accessModes` | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.accessModes` | **No** | | | `*.persistence.selector` / claims selector | `volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.selector` | **No** | | | `*.persistence.labels` / VCT labels & name | `volumeClaimTemplates` identity | **No** | Renames/label changes on VCT block upgrades | | `*.podManagementPolicy` | `spec.podManagementPolicy` | **No** | | | `*.selectorLabels` (pod selector) | `spec.selector` | **No** | Extremely disruptive if changed | | service / headless naming that feeds `serviceName` | `spec.serviceName` | **No** | | | Most `*.persistence.annotations` (on VCT) | `volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata.annotations` | Often **No** | Depends on K8s/version; treat as risky | | Pod template: image, resources, env, probes, affinity, volumes (non-VCT), etc. | `spec.template` | **Yes** | Prefer these for day-2 changes | | `replicas`, `updateStrategy`, PVC retention policy, `minReadySeconds` | corresponding STS top-level fields | **Yes** | Per Kubernetes STS update rules | Please treat the table as a starting checklist maintainers can correct against current templates under `production/helm/loki/templates/**/statefulset*.yaml`. #### 2) Prefer template-only (mutable) knobs for day-2 ops In docs, explicitly recommend: - Prefer changes that land only in `spec.template` (config via ConfigMap/Secret hashes, resources, probes, env, extraVolumes that are not VCT-backed, etc.). - Treat storage class, PVC size, access modes, VCT labels/selectors, `podManagementPolicy`, and selector labels as **install-time** decisions unless a documented migration is followed. #### 3) Migration notes for `volumeClaimTemplates` / storage Document supported operator procedures when an immutable field *must* change, e.g.: - **PVC size increase (Single Binary):** `singleBinary.persistence.enableStatefulSetRecreationForSizeChange` and the recreate Job path — when to enable, risks, and prerequisites (storage class allowing expansion, etc.). - **storageClass / accessModes / selector changes:** safe sequence such as: 1. Ensure object storage / backup strategy is sound (filesystem single-binary vs object-storage backends). 2. Scale down or pause ingestion if required. 3. Delete StatefulSet with `cascade=orphan` (or chart-supported recreate) so PVCs are retained when intended. 4. Recreate STS with new VCT fields / re-attach or migrate data. 5. Resume traffic. - **Chart upgrades that rewrite VCT fields** (historical `#19065`-style): call out in upgrade notes when default templates change immutable fields, and whether operators must delete/recreate STS or pin values for compatibility. #### 4) GitOps / server-side apply notes (Flux, Argo, etc.) Add a short “Continuous delivery” callout: - Immutable STS field drift will fail every reconcile, not only one-shot `helm upgrade`. - Avoid oscillating values that rewrite VCT (e.g. default `null` storageClass vs explicit class) across environments. - Under server-side apply / field managers, also watch for chart-generated VCT `apiVersion`/`kind` or defaulted fields that differ from live objects and surface as forbidden updates (see past MinIO/STS defaulting issues in this chart family). - Suggested operational pattern: fail closed on immutable changes (manual approval / freeze HelmRelease) rather than retry-spam. ### Describe alternatives you've considered 1. **Rely only on Kubernetes error messages** — insufficient; does not map errors back to Helm values. 2. **Delete/recreate STS ad hoc** — works but is tribal knowledge; risky without chart-specific guidance (PVC retention, ring membership, WAL/data dirs). 3. **Use `enableStatefulSetRecreationForSizeChange` only** — currently narrow (size, Single Binary-oriented); does not cover storageClass/accessModes/selectors or all STS components. 4. **File only one-off bugs when a chart release changes an immutable field** — necessary, but does not reduce operator confusion between releases. ### Additional context **Minimal reproduce (generic):** ```bash # namespace example only — no cluster-specific names beyond monitoring/loki helm upgrade --install loki grafana/loki \ --namespace monitoring \ --create-namespace \ --set deploymentMode=SingleBinary \ --set singleBinary.replicas=1 \ --set singleBinary.persistence.enabled=true \ --set singleBinary.persistence.size=10Gi # ... storage backend values as appropriate ... # later: change an immutable-bound value helm upgrade loki grafana/loki \ --namespace monitoring \ --reuse-values \ --set singleBinary.persistence.storageClass=standard-rwo # or change accessModes / selector / podManagementPolicy / VCT labels ``` Observed: Helm reports StatefulSet update forbidden; under Flux the `HelmRelease` stays failing on each reconcile. **Why docs matter here:** the chart already exposes many STS-affecting knobs (`persistence.*`, `podManagementPolicy`, `selectorLabels`, VCT labels/annotations, claims arrays for distributed components). Operators and GitOps users need a single authoritative “do not change after install / how to migrate” page rather than discovering via failed applies. Happy to review a PR that only adds documentation; chart validation (e.g. NOTES.txt warning, or CI fixture detecting immutable field diffs) would be a welcome follow-up but is not required for this request.

signal.title: pattern tee: nil-pointer panic in distributor - TenantConfigs nil because PatternIngesterTee lacks TenantConfigs module dependency
signal.text: ## Describe the bug Distributors intermittently panic (SIGSEGV) in the pattern-ingester tee path. The panic is a nil dereference of `*runtime.TenantConfigs` inside `TeeService`. It is non-deterministic per pod: some distributor pods start, serve traffic, then crash once with `exit=2`, and usually recover on restart. ## Environment - Loki: **3.5.2** (also verified in source: v3.5.3, v3.5.5, `main`) - Mode: distributed / microservices (separate `distributor` target) - `auth_enabled: false` (single tenant `fake`) - `pattern_ingester.enabled: true` - `runtime_config` effectively empty (`{}`) ## Stack trace ``` panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x299258c] runtime.(*TenantConfigs).getOverridesForUser(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:80 runtime.(*TenantConfigs).LogPushRequestStreams(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:98 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch.func1(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:347 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:299 pattern.(*TeeService).batchSender(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:279 pattern.(*TeeService).Start.func1() pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:120 created by pattern.(*TeeService).Start pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:119 ``` ## Root cause (analysis) - `getOverridesForUser` (pkg/runtime/config.go) panics because the receiver `*TenantConfigs` (`ts.tenantCfgs`) is `nil`, not because the provider is nil. - `initPatternIngesterTee` builds the tee with `t.tenantConfigs` (pkg/loki/modules.go), but the module dependency graph does **not** list `TenantConfigs` as a dependency of `PatternIngesterTee`: ``` PatternIngesterTee: {Server, Overrides, MemberlistKV, Analytics, PatternRingClient} ``` So depending on module init order, `t.tenantConfigs` can still be `nil` when the tee is constructed. The tee stores it as-is and later dereferences it in the async `batchSender` goroutine (`tee_service.go`), with no nil guard. - This is distinct from the already-merged fixes #14665 (added `Overrides` dep, 3.3.0) and #16112 (initialize overrides for pattern tee, 3.5.0): those address the `Overrides` object, not `TenantConfigs`. - Verified the gap persists in v3.5.2, v3.5.3, v3.5.5 and `main`: `PatternIngesterTee` still omits `TenantConfigs`, and `NewTeeService` / `sendBatch` still dereference `tenantCfgs` without a nil check. ## Impact - Distributor process crash -> transient 5xx on in-flight pushes (clients retry to other distributors; effective log loss ~0), pod churn, HPA jitter. - Only the patterns write path is affected; normal ingest and queries are fine. ## Suggested fix Either (or both): 1. Add `TenantConfigs` to the `PatternIngesterTee` dependencies in `setupModuleManager` so `t.tenantConfigs` is initialized before the tee is built. 2. Add a nil guard in `TeeService` before calling `ts.tenantCfgs.LogPushRequestStreams(...)`. ## Workaround Set `pattern_ingester.enabled: false` (the tee is gated by `if !Pattern.Enabled`), which removes the tee and the panic.
signal.author: HDMAUROB

signal.title: approx_topk() fails with parse error when using operator's custom LogQL parser
signal.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** In the Loki Operator, when using `approx_topk()` with a custom LogQL parser setup (Observatorium API gateway), queries fail with a syntax error. The error originates from the query-frontend pod, not from the custom gateway/parser. Other newly added LogQL functions (like `variants()`) work correctly through the same setup, and `approx_topk()` works in standalone Loki installations. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Provision kubernetes or OpenShift cluster 2. Deploy Loki Operator with: - custom operator image, built from: https://github.com/btaani/loki/tree/enable_multi_variant_queries - custom Observatorium API gateway (`quay.io/btaani/api:new-logql-features-83d0dd0-multiarch`) 3. Deploy Loki components using image: `grafana/loki:3.7.3` (also tested with `grafana/loki:3.6.5` and `grafana/loki:latest`) 4. Query using logcli: ```bash export LOKI_ADDR="https://<your lokistack address>/api/logs/v1/application" export LOKI_BEARER_TOKEN="$(oc whoami -t)" export LOKI_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY="true" logcli instant-query 'approx_topk(3, bytes_over_time({kubernetes_namespace_name="<any app namespace>"}[1m]))' ``` 5. Observe error: ```bash parse error at line 1, col 1: syntax error: unexpected IDENTIFIER (<nil>) attempts remaining: 0 Query failed: run out of attempts while querying the server ``` exact error on the query-frontend pod: ```bash level=info ts=2026-07-08T12:52:51.221017611Z caller=roundtrip.go:412 org_id=application msg="executing query" type=instant query="approx_topk(3, bytes_over_time({kubernetes_namespace_name=\"log-test-0\"}[1m]))" query_hash=353573704 level=warn ts=2026-07-08T12:52:51.225403372Z caller=retry.go:125 org_id=application msg="received an error but not a retryable code, this is possibly a bug." code=Code(400) err="rpc error: code = Code(400) desc = parse error at line 1, col 1: syntax error: unexpected IDENTIFIER" ``` **Expected behavior** The approx_topk query should execute successfully and return results similar to how it works in standalone Loki installations **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (OpenShift) - Deployment tool: Operator - Loki versions tested: v3.6.5, v3.7.3, latest (all exhibit same behavior) - Query path: logcli → Observatorium API gateway (with custom parser) → query-frontend → querier - Custom parser implementation of approx_topk: https://github.com/btaani/api/tree/new-logql-features - Operator image used: https://github.com/btaani/loki/tree/enable_multi_variant_queries

signal.title: ruler.evaluation.query_frontend gRPC client message size appears configurable via flags only, not via YAML and limits to 4MiB
signal.text: **Describe the bug** Hello, I am running loki 3.7.3 and using the ruler to aggregate netflow logs to metrics. however i receive these error messages very frequently. So I asked AI to understand the issue and it seems to be a 4MB limit because the variable has different syntax or is not available in the YAML configuration and does not use the configured limit from the loki.yml. This is the AI summary: `rule evaluation failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (5054383 vs. 4194304) ` This happens on the remote evaluation path of the ruler. From the code, the relevant parts seem to be: Loki: `pkg/ruler/evaluator_remote.go` especially: ``` DialQueryFrontend() QueryFrontendConfig (*RemoteEvaluator).query() ``` dskit: ``` grpcclient/grpcclient.go especially: type Config struct RegisterFlagsWithPrefix() CallOptions() DialOption() ``` Relevant source files: https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/pkg/ruler/evaluator_remote.go https://github.com/grafana/dskit/blob/main/grpcclient/grpcclient.go QueryFrontendConfig embeds grpcclient.Config: ``` type QueryFrontendConfig struct { Address string `yaml:"address"` ClientConfig grpcclient.Config `yaml:",inline"` } ``` and registers flags via: `c.ClientConfig.RegisterFlagsWithPrefix("ruler.evaluation.query-frontend", f) ` However, in our setup, YAML fields like these are rejected: ``` ruler: evaluation: query_frontend: max_recv_msg_size: 16777216 max_send_msg_size: 16777216 grpc_compression: snappy connect_timeout: 5s ``` with errors like: ``` field max_recv_msg_size not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field max_send_msg_size not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field grpc_compression not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig field connect_timeout not found in type ruler.QueryFrontendConfig ``` At the same time, the corresponding CLI flags appear to exist: ``` -ruler.evaluation.query-frontend.grpc-max-recv-msg-size -ruler.evaluation.query-frontend.grpc-max-send-msg-size ``` So it looks like the gRPC client settings for ruler.evaluation.query_frontend are exposed via flags, but not actually accepted via YAML config. Could you please clarify whether this is expected? If not, it seems something is missing around YAML unmarshalling / inlining for QueryFrontendConfig and its embedded grpcclient.Config. signal.title: Automatically set GOMEMLIMIT from the cgroup memory limit at runtime (adopt automemlimit)
signal.text: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Today Loki relies on a manually configured, static GOMEMLIMIT to keep the Go runtime's memory usage under the container memory limit and avoid OOM kills. This is fragile because GOMEMLIMIT and the actual container memory limit can easily drift out of sync. Changing the container's resources.limits.memory through any path other than the Helm value (e.g. a Kustomize overlay, a manually patched manifest, VPA, or a non-Helm deployment) does not update GOMEMLIMIT. The Go runtime keeps using the stale value. The result is either OOM kills (limit lowered, GOMEMLIMIT still high) or overly aggressive GC / wasted memory (limit raised, GOMEMLIMIT still low). Components like the query-frontend are especially sensitive to this because their memory usage is bursty and GC-tunable, so a stale GOMEMLIMIT directly translates into OOMs. **Describe the solution you'd like** Have Loki set GOMEMLIMIT automatically at runtime from the cgroup memory limit, using a configurable percentage, by adopting [github.com/KimMachineGun/automemlimit](https://github.com/KimMachineGun/automemlimit). Concretely: - Initialize automemlimit early in Loki's main (cmd/loki) so it runs before the app starts. - Respect an explicit GOMEMLIMIT if the user has already set one (automemlimit is a no-op when GOMEMLIMIT is set). - Allow tuning the fraction via AUTOMEMLIMIT (e.g. default 0.9, or align with the chart's existing 0.85). **Describe alternatives you've considered** Manual static GOMEMLIMIT env var: no percentage support and must be manually kept in sync with the limit.
signal.author: zoelandeyro

signal.title: Proposal: Add native OCI Object Storage support via Thanos objstore.
signal.text: ## Problem Loki does not currently expose OCI Object Storage as a supported Thanos object-store backend. OCI users therefore have to use the S3-compatible API and static Customer Secret Keys. This prevents using OCI-native authentication mechanisms such as: - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal - Resource Principal ## Proposed solution Add `oci` to Loki's Thanos object-store backends by reusing the OCI provider from Thanos objstore. Proposed configuration: ``` storage_config: use_thanos_objstore: true object_store: oci: provider: instance-principal bucket: loki-data region: ap-tokyo-1 max_request_retries: 3 request_retry_interval: 1 schema_config: configs: - from: 2026-08-01 store: tsdb object_store: oci schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ``` ## Security benefit No OCI Customer Secret Key needs to be stored in Loki configuration or Kubernetes Secrets. ## Scope - Loki TSDB object storage - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal - Unit tests - OCI/OKE integration test documentation Named stores and Helm chart support can be submitted separately. ## Validation A standalone Thanos OCI client has already been validated successfully against OCI Object Storage from OKE using Instance Principal.

signal.title: Volume API and index stats over-report after log deletion; log queries stay correct
signal.text: **Describe the bug** After the compactor processes a delete request (filter-and-delete), `/loki/api/v1/index/volume` and `/loki/api/v1/index/stats` over-report the affected streams for hours, while log/metric queries (`bytes_over_time` etc.) remain exact throughout. A second delete against the same stream selector roughly doubles the namespace's index references, inflating even query windows that are disjoint from every deleted range. The inflation survives pod restarts and does not converge within hours. This matters to anyone composing the Volume API with the delete API for per-tenant/per-namespace usage accounting: after the first delete, volume readings for that stream set can no longer be trusted. **To Reproduce** Loki 3.7.4, single binary, filesystem object store, TSDB v13 schema, `auth_enabled: false`. Compactor settings tightened only to shorten the wait: `compaction_interval: 2m`, `delete_request_cancel_period: 1m`, `retention_delete_delay: 5m`. 1. Push ~30 MB of synthetic logs (3 streams, one `namespace` label value, timestamps spread over the past 6 h), then `POST /flush`. 2. Baseline agrees: instant volume query reports 29.95 MB vs 30.18 MB ground truth from `sum(bytes_over_time(...[7h]))` (−0.8%). 3. `POST /loki/api/v1/delete` for the oldest 3 h of that namespace; wait until the request lists as `processed`. 4. `bytes_over_time` immediately reports the expected 14.84 MB (exact). The volume query for the same selector/window reports **68.1 MB**, decays stepwise (39.9 → 6.6 MB over ~10 min), then sticks at ~1.9× truth. Restarting the pod does not clear it (it read 10.6 MB after a restart). `index/stats` at that point returns **17 streams / 16,201 entries** where the actual remaining data is 3 streams / 6,946 lines. 5. Issue a second delete for part of the remaining range. After it processes, index references for the whole namespace roughly **double** (2,359 chunks / 11.16 M entries vs a clean-baseline 1,176 / 5.99 M), and a volume query restricted to a window disjoint from both deleted ranges reports ~**2.03×** its `bytes_over_time` truth, flat for 14+ minutes. A larger second dataset (3.018 GB, 6 streams) reproduced the same shape: pre-delete volume/truth ratio 1.017; after one delete a window past the deleted range stayed byte-stable; after a second delete the whole namespace's refs doubled. **Expected behavior** Volume/stats either apply delete-request filtering the way log queries do, or the docs state that these endpoints are not deletion-aware. **Root cause (from reading v3.7.4 source; code paths unchanged on `main` as of 2026-08-05)** 1. `SelectLogs`/`SelectSamples` inject pending (and recently completed) delete requests as query-time filters (`pkg/querier/querier.go`), which is why log queries stay exact through the index-cleanup transient. `IndexStats` and `Volume` in the same file take no delete parameters at all — the transient is exposed raw. 2. The querier's volume also sums the ingester's in-memory contribution (`pkg/ingester/instance.go`, unflushed chunks), which is delete-blind and WAL-durable — hence restart-proof inflation that decays as chunks flush. 3. In single-binary, the index view merges the compactor-rewritten object-store index with ingester-uploaded head TSDBs (`indexshipper` iterates the uploads manager too), which the compactor's delete processing never rewrites and which are retained for `IndexCacheValidity + 3×ResyncInterval`; the volume aggregation (`ChunkStats` summing `ChunkMeta.KB`, with pre-aggregated page markers) has no chunk-identity dedup across the merged sources, so rewritten chunks and their stale predecessors are counted together. **Environment** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (k3d), grafana-community helm chart 18.5.2 - Deployment tool: helm - Loki 3.7.4 (also inspected current `main`), single binary, filesystem object store, TSDB v13 I'm not asking for a commitment to fix — filing so the behavior is documented and searchable, since we could find no existing issue covering it. Happy to provide the full reproduction scripts.

signal.title: docs: Note that index/stats and index/volume are not deletion-aware
signal.text: Documents the caveat reported in #23807. `SelectLogs` and `SelectSamples` pass the filters from pending and recently processed delete requests into the query via `deletion.DeletesForUserQuery` (`pkg/querier/querier.go`), so log and metric queries are exact as soon as a delete request is processed. `IndexStats` and `Volume` in the same file take no delete parameters — they report what the index holds, so the same stream selector can keep reporting deleted data until the compactor has rewritten the index and the pre-rewrite index files have aged out. `Volume` also fans out to the ingesters, whose not-yet-flushed chunks are counted before any delete filtering applies to them, while `IndexStats` is store-only. The reference already carries a caveats list for `index/stats`; this adds the deletion caveat there and an equivalent note on `index/volume` / `index/volume_range`, which had none. It also points at `bytes_over_time` for accounting that has to be exact, since that path is deletion-aware. This is documentation only. The reporter's second ask — making these endpoints deletion-aware, or deduplicating chunk identity across the merged compactor-rewritten and ingester-uploaded index views — is a behaviour change I did not want to guess at, so I have left it to #23807. Verified against `main`: the delete-parameter asymmetry between `SelectLogs`/`SelectSamples` and `IndexStats`/`Volume` is still present, and `Volume` still queries the ingesters.

signal.title: feat(logql): Evaluate approx_count_distinct with HyperLogLog
signal.text: ## Summary Second slice of experimental `approx_count_distinct` ([grafana/loki-private#2769](https://github.com/grafana/loki-private/issues/2769)). Stacked on #24112. This PR teaches the querier engine to evaluate `LabelAggregationExpr` locally and return a normal PromQL vector of HyperLogLog estimates. Instant queries only. Sketch emission, shard merge, protobuf transport, and the feature gate are later PRs. ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` ## How it wires to #24112 #24112 added the syntax and the extractor, but the engine still treated `LabelAggregationExpr` as an unknown sample expression. 1. The parser still produces `LabelAggregationExpr`. 2. `DefaultEvaluator.NewStepEvaluator` now handles that type. It calls `SelectSamples` with the AST in the query plan, using the same `(T-D-O, T-O]` window as range aggregations. 3. Store and ingester already call `expr.Extractor()` from #24112, so they emit xxhash64 bits in `Sample.Value` and labels reduced to the `by (...)` set. 4. The step evaluator groups those samples by the exact serialized label string, `InsertHash`s into `hyperloglog.New14()`, and returns `Estimate()` as a `SampleVector`. `CountDistinctSketchExpr` remains parseable in query plans from #24112 but is still not evaluated here. Returning mergeable sketches is part of the sharding PR. ## Roadmap 1. Syntax, AST, extractor (#24112) 2. **This PR** — local HLL estimates on a querier 3. Shard + sketch eval + protobuf transport (merge-before-estimate) 4. Feature gate + result-cache bypass 5. Docs ## What to check - Only `LabelAggregationExpr` is wired; `CountDistinctSketchExpr` still hits `EvaluatorUnsupportedType`. - Grouping uses exact label strings, not a hash, so two groups cannot collapse. - Instant-only is enforced before any scan; range queries error here, not only in a later gate PR. - Bounds in `TestApproxCountDistinctBoundaries` match range aggregations: `(T-D, T]`. ## Risks This PR makes evaluation work on a **querier** (direct `/query`, or a frontend that forwards the original AST unchanged). The public result is a normal PromQL vector of estimates. The default query-frontend path still fails. `querier.parallelise-shardable-queries` defaults to true, and `ShardMapper` has no `LabelAggregationExpr` case, so mapping returns `unexpected expr type` before any querier runs. ## Test plan - [x] `go test ./pkg/logql/`

signal.title: [helm] Zone-aware ingester StatefulSets emit a duplicate `name` label and become invalid when `ingester.podLabels.name` is set
signal.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** When `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`, the three zone StatefulSet templates use the pod label `name: <prefix>ingester-zone-{a,b,c}` as the zone discriminator, and reference it from `spec.selector.matchLabels`. The same templates also append `.Values.loki.podLabels` and `.Values.ingester.podLabels` verbatim via `toYaml`, *after* their own labels and without merging. If a user sets `podLabels.name`, the rendered `spec.template.metadata.labels` therefore contains the key `name` **twice**. Two consequences: 1. The chart emits a YAML mapping with a duplicate key, which is invalid per the YAML spec regardless of what the user supplied. 2. Duplicate keys resolve last-wins, so the effective pod label becomes the user's value while `spec.selector.matchLabels` still requires the chart's. The API server rejects the StatefulSet with `` `selector` does not match template `labels` ``. The same key is also used by the per-zone headless Services (`service-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}-headless.yaml`), so a naive workaround of dropping the chart's label would leave those Services with no endpoints and break stable pod DNS. The non-zone-aware template is not affected: its selector is only `loki.ingesterSelectorLabels` and does not include `name`, so overriding `podLabels.name` there is harmless. The inconsistency looks unintentional — the zone templates added `name` to the selector without protecting it from the override path the chart itself exposes. `rollout-group` and the `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are exposed to the same collision. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0 (Loki 3.3.2). 2. Render the zone-a ingester StatefulSet with `podLabels.name` set: ```yaml # values.yaml deploymentMode: Distributed loki: storage: type: s3 bucketNames: chunks: chunks ruler: ruler admin: admin schemaConfig: configs: - from: "2024-04-01" store: tsdb object_store: s3 schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ingester: replicas: 3 podLabels: name: my-ingester # any value collides zoneAwareReplication: enabled: true read: replicas: 0 write: replicas: 0 backend: replicas: 0 ``` ``` helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.25.0 -f values.yaml \ -s templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-a.yaml ``` 3. Apply the rendered manifest to a cluster. **Expected behavior** The chart should never emit a mapping with a duplicate key, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` should always be a subset of `spec.template.metadata.labels` for any user-supplied `podLabels`. Either the chart's structurally significant labels should win over user-supplied `podLabels`, or the chart should reject the conflicting configuration with a clear message. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes 1.34 (EKS), also reproducible with `helm template` alone - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0, Loki 3.3.2) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Rendered output, `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true` — note `name` appears twice in `template.metadata.labels`, and the selector requires the first value: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a # <-- selector requires this rollout-group: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: ingester-zone-a # <-- chart's label rollout-group: ingester name: my-ingester # <-- duplicate key, wins ``` The per-zone headless Service selects on the same key: ```yaml # service-ingester-zone-a-headless.yaml selector: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a rollout-group: ingester ``` Same values with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=false` — single `name`, and the selector does not reference it, so nothing breaks: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: my-ingester ``` `kubectl apply` of the zone-aware manifest fails with: ``` The StatefulSet "loki-ingester-zone-a" is invalid: spec.template.metadata.labels: Invalid value: map[string]string{"app.kubernetes.io/component":"ingester", "app.kubernetes.io/instance":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/name":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/part-of":"memberlist", "name":"my-ingester", "rollout-group":"ingester"}: `selector` does not match template `labels` ``` --- ## Proposed fix `spec.selector` is immutable on a StatefulSet, so changing the discriminator to a dedicated key (e.g. `zone: zone-a`) would force existing zone-aware deployments to recreate their ingester StatefulSets. The options below keep the selector as it is. **Option 1 — merge the label sets so each key is emitted once (preferred).** In `templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}.yaml`, replace the `labels:` block under `spec.template.metadata` with a single merged dict, chart labels taking precedence (sprig `merge` gives precedence to the destination): ```gotemplate labels: {{- $zoneLabels := dict "app.kubernetes.io/part-of" "memberlist" "name" (printf "%singester-zone-a" (include "loki.prefixIngesterName" .)) "rollout-group" (printf "%singester" (include "loki.prefixRolloutGroup" .)) }} {{- $userLabels := merge (deepCopy (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict)) (.Values.loki.podLabels | default dict) }} {{- toYaml (merge $zoneLabels $userLabels (fromYaml (include "loki.ingesterSelectorLabels" .))) | nindent 8 }} ``` This emits every key once and guarantees `selector ⊆ labels` for any `podLabels`. Users keep the ability to add their own labels; they simply cannot silently break the selector. **Option 2 — minimal reordering.** Move the two `podLabels` blocks *above* the chart's `name` and `rollout-group` lines, so the chart's values are emitted last and win. This fixes the selector mismatch with a three-line diff, but still emits a duplicate key, so it only addresses the second consequence. **Option 3 — fail fast (complementary to either of the above).** Reject the conflicting configuration explicitly rather than rendering something that the API server will refuse: ```gotemplate {{- if and .Values.ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled (hasKey (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict) "name") }} {{- fail "ingester.podLabels may not set 'name' when ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled is true: that label is the zone discriminator used by the StatefulSet selector and the per-zone headless Services" }} {{- end }} ``` Whichever option is taken, documenting `name`, `rollout-group` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` as reserved keys under `ingester.podLabels` in `values.yaml` would help. **Workaround for anyone hitting this now** Do not set `ingester.podLabels.name` with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`. If the label is required (for example a metrics pipeline that relabels from the pod label `name`), the selector and the three per-zone headless Services have to be post-processed consistently onto a different discriminator key — all four objects must agree, or the Services lose their endpoints and stable pod DNS breaks.
