signal.title: Tailing leaks BaseLabelsBuilder.resultCache — regression of #6152, reintroduced by #9949
signal.text: ## Summary `pipeline.Reset()` does not clear `BaseLabelsBuilder.resultCache`, so a long-lived ingester tailer accumulates one cached `LabelsResult` per distinct label set for the lifetime of the tail session. With structured metadata (which OTLP ingestion produces by default) the label set differs per entry, so the cache grows without bound. This is a regression. #6152 (2022) fixed exactly this by rebuilding the pipeline on every push; #9949 (2023) replaced that with `t.pipeline.Reset()`, which only clears `streamPipelines`. The gap has been present since 2.9.0 and is still in v3.7.6 and `main`. ## The regression #6152 added the guard, and its description names the failure precisely: > The query pipeline will build a label cache to improve performance when processing queries, > the normal use of a pipeline for queries is ephemeral so the cache is cleared when the > pipeline is discarded. When tailing, however, the pipeline was long lived and reused which > lead to an unbounded growth of cached labels for certain tail queries. This PR creates a new > pipeline for every processed push into Loki vs reusing. There is probably future potential > for a mechanism to clear the cache but not sure it's worth the additional effort vs creating > and disposing of pipelines. ```go + // Build a new pipeline for each call because the pipeline builds a cache of labels + // and if we don't start with a new pipeline that cache will grow unbounded. + pipeline, _ := t.expr.Pipeline() ``` #9949 removed it: ```diff - // Build a new pipeline for each call because the pipeline builds a cache of labels - // and if we don't start with a new pipeline that cache will grow unbounded. - pipeline, _ := t.expr.Pipeline() + // Reset the pipeline caches so they don't grow unbounded + t.pipeline.Reset() ``` But `Reset()` does not clear the cache the comment refers to. `pkg/logql/log/pipeline.go`: ```go func (p *pipeline) Reset() { p.mu.Lock() defer p.mu.Unlock() p.baseBuilder.Reset() for k := range p.streamPipelines { delete(p.streamPipelines, k) } } ``` `pkg/logql/log/labels.go`: ```go func (b *BaseLabelsBuilder) Reset() { b.del = b.del[:0] for k := range b.add { b.add[k] = b.add[k][:0] } b.err = "" b.errDetails = "" b.baseMap = nil b.parserKeyHints.Reset() } ``` `resultCache` is written in three places and never deleted from: ```go b.resultCache[hash] = result ``` ## Why structured metadata makes it unbounded `streamPipeline.Process` adds structured metadata to the builder for every entry: ```go func (p *streamPipeline) Process(ts int64, line []byte, structuredMetadata labels.Labels) ([]byte, LabelsResult, bool) { p.builder.Reset() p.builder.Add(StructuredMetadataLabel, structuredMetadata) ... } ``` This makes `hasAdd()` true, so `LabelsResult()` never takes the unchanged-labels fast path and always inserts into `resultCache`. The cache key is the hash of the full label set including structured metadata, so any per-entry-varying value (trace id, span id, request id) yields one cache entry per log line. ## Reproduction Against tag v3.7.1, driving a pipeline the way `tailer.processStream` does (calling `Reset()` between batches): ``` TestReproA {app="x"} | json after batch 0 ( 100 lines): resultCache = 101 after batch 9 (1000 lines): resultCache = 1001 TestReproB {app="x"} |= "foo", entries carry trace_id in structured metadata after batch 9 (1000 lines): resultCache = 1001 TestReproC control: line filter only, no structured metadata resultCache = 1 ``` Retention cost measured with six realistic labels plus a 32-character trace id: ``` resultCache entries = 200001 retained per entry = 595 bytes ``` A line filter alone is enough — a parser stage is not required — as long as structured metadata is present. ## Production impact Loki 3.7.1, distributed mode, OTLP ingestion (schema v13), 6 ingesters at 16Gi each, about 157 MiB/s ingested. Live heap from one ingester, `go tool pprof -inuse_space`: ``` flat flat% sum% cum cum% 4921.98MB 44.90% 44.90% 4921.98MB 44.90% bytes.(*Buffer).String 4402.99MB 40.16% 85.06% 4402.99MB 40.16% github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/labels.New ``` The call chain is single-parent at every hop, 100 percent attributed: ``` ingester.(*tailer).receiveStreamsLoop -> ingester.(*tailer).processStream 9336.58MB 85.16% -> logql/log.(*streamPipeline).ProcessString -> logql/log.(*streamPipeline).Process -> logql/log.(*LabelsBuilder).LabelsResult -> labels.Labels.String -> bytes.(*Buffer).String -> labels.New ``` Six ingesters entered an OOMKill loop. Sibling stacks in the same cluster, same image, same chart, same canary configuration, and a comparable number of tail sessions, but without churn, show no allocation at all on this path and sit at about 2 GiB. ## Orphaned tailers make it permanent `processStream` returns early when the pipeline is a noop, so a plain selector costs nothing. The cost lands on tailers whose pipeline is not noop, and those tailers are not always cleaned up. After restarting every querier in the cluster, the ingester still held 14 tailers whose goroutines had been blocked in `receiveStreamsLoop` since the restart: ``` 32 select <- active 26 select, 5 minutes <- orphaned 2 select, 6 minutes <- orphaned ``` Tail path live heap before the querier restart, and at two points after: ``` before : 9336.58 MB (85.16%) T+90s : 3679.91 MB (65.54%) T+5min : 3679.91 MB (58.81%) byte-identical, not reclaimed ``` Ingester-side tailer cleanup is reactive — it depends on the gRPC stream closing. When a querier goes away without a clean close, the tailer goroutine and its `resultCache` survive with nothing to release them, and there is no timeout-based reaper. Each churn event leaves more of them behind, so the footprint ratchets upward until the ingester is killed. ## Suggested fix Clearing the cache in `BaseLabelsBuilder.Reset()` restores the invariant #6152 established and matches what the #9949 comment already claims: ```go func (b *BaseLabelsBuilder) Reset() { b.del = b.del[:0] for k := range b.add { b.add[k] = b.add[k][:0] } b.err = "" b.errDetails = "" b.baseMap = nil b.parserKeyHints.Reset() + clear(b.resultCache) } ``` This costs the query path its cross-`Reset()` cache reuse, so bounding the cache instead of clearing it may be preferable. Separately, a timeout-based reaper for ingester tailers would stop orphans from retaining whatever bound is chosen. ## Environment - Loki 3.7.1, distributed mode, Helm chart 13.2.0 - schema v13, OTLP ingestion, unmapped resource attributes stored as structured metadata - `max_concurrent_tail_requests: 20` - loki-canary as a DaemonSet, one tail session per node Verified unchanged in v3.7.6 and `main`: `pkg/ingester/tailer.go` and `pkg/logql/log/labels.go` are byte-identical to v3.7.1. ## Related - #6152 — original fix - #9949 — regression - #21524 — notes `resultCache` in a thread-safety context, assumes `Reset()` addressed the growth - #8635 — open since 2023, parser tails causing stream-map blowup, same underlying behaviour - #13123 / #13146 — different path (symbolizer retaining gRPC buffers), already fixed ## Template mapping Filed without the bug-report template; mapping for triage. - **Describe the bug** — see Summary. - **To Reproduce** — see Reproduction. Loki v3.7.1; the Go test drives `pipeline.Reset()` the way `tailer.processStream` does and counts `resultCache` entries. - **Expected behavior** — `pipeline.Reset()` should leave the tailer's pipeline in the state a freshly built pipeline would be in, as it did before #9949. Concretely, `resultCache` should not retain entries across `Reset()`, so a long-lived tailer's memory stays bounded regardless of how many distinct label sets it has processed. - **Environment** — Kubernetes, Helm chart 13.2.0, distributed mode, OTLP ingestion with schema v13. Full details in the Environment section above. - **Screenshots, config, or terminal output** — pprof output inline above.

signal.title: indexgateway: Cap client-side in-flight requests to avoid retry amplification when all replicas shed
signal.text: With -index-gateway.max-concurrent enabled, GatewayClient.poolDo retries a shed request against the next replica, which is the behavior we want: another replica may be less loaded. When every replica is saturated the same mechanism amplifies load. poolDo passes maxRetries = -1 for six of the seven RPCs, so it walks the entire address set, and in simple mode that set is every discovered gateway. A single request can therefore wait up to max-concurrent-queue-timeout per replica before failing, and each of those waits occupies a queue slot on a gateway that is already overloaded. A client-side cap on in-flight index gateway requests would let the client fail fast once it can see the whole pool is shedding, instead of serially probing every replica. Follow-up to https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/23932.
signal.author: trevorwhitney

signal.title: Metric queries and log queries cover different time ranges for the same request
signal.text: Log queries and histogram queries with `count_over_time` produce two different windows for the same time range and the counts don't always match. ### Steps to reproduce In our dev env, window `09:51:56.691Z` -> `09:51:57.557Z` (866ms): ``` log query {service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" -> 113 lines metric sum(count_over_time({service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" [100ms])) step=100ms -> buckets at .600 .700 .800 .900 .000 .100 .200 .300 .400 .500 -> sum = 138 ``` I pulled every line in the area and checked by hand. Of those 138, **27 fall before the window start** and **2 lines inside the window are missing** because there's no bucket for them. ### Why Two things stack up. Step alignment rounds both start and end *down* to a step multiple (`queryrangebase/step_align.go:20-23`). So `.691` becomes `.600` and `.557` becomes `.500`. That alone pulls in extra data at the front and drops data off the back. Then the first bucket counts `(t - step, t]`, so it reaches back another full step behind the already-rounded start (`logql/range_vector.go:155`, `engine/internal/executor/range_aggregation.go:41-51`). Net effect, for a request of `[start, end)`: ``` actually covered: (floor(start/step)*step - step, floor(end/step)*step] ``` Up to 2 steps of extra data at the front, up to 1 step missing at the back. Log queries don't get any of this. `engine/handler.go:180-183` skips them on purpose to preserve sub-second precision, and the log splitter doesn't align either. So the two query types genuinely answer questions about different windows. ### Impact Logs Drilldown sums the volume histogram client-side and shows it next to the log line count, with no clipping (`LogsVolumePanel.tsx:146`). Users see two numbers that should match and don't. Tracked from the UI side in grafana/logs-drilldown#2049.

signal.title: enable --envproxy by default
signal.text: <!-- I changed the structure here since this is less a feature request and more a flag change. --> **Context on `--envproxy`** In #14950 I added the --envproxy flag to LogCLI. This means HTTP_PROXY args are followed, allowing a transparent proxy. Back in issue #11742 I mentioned that I think this should be default behaviour. Well, I didn't continue that thread afterwards - because in practice when you set HTTP_PROXY, you may also be setting SSL_CERTS_FILE. And that had [a bug in darwin/windows](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/77865) which meant TLS would ultimately not work. My thinking was since you needed `--tls-skip-verify`, `--envproxy` be default would cause more problems than it was worth by default. With Go 1.27.0, this issue is fixed! **Why change?** By we changed the default envproxy behaviour, proxied environments (or auth wrappers) will need no extra configuration to "just work". It matches the behaviour of other popular CLI tools like `curl`, and those that rely on `libcurl` (although using SSL_CERTS on darwin curl goes through system SSL, but that's beside the point). **Could this break anything?** Technically yes: if somebody is running some logcli scripts in a environment where they have this PROXY set, but don't intend for them to be used. I think in almost all cases this is a mistake, so a brief mention of that change in a CHANGELOG would be enough. Given that most modern CLI tools have this behaviour, it feels as if logcli should too. It reduces the burden of users of the tool. If folks agree, when the 1.27 upgrade is done, can we also change this flag? Maybe this would need to be included in a version bump, though. I am not clear on the loki standards for versioning.

signal.title: Regression (3.6.0+): compactor retention fails on boltdb-shipper chunks spanning an index-period boundary ("could not find entry of chunk ... to remove it")
signal.text: ## Summary Since **v3.6.0**, compactor retention with a `boltdb-shipper` schema fails to delete any chunk whose time range spans an index-period (table) boundary, and — because one table error aborts the whole run — this blocks retention entirely. `loki_compactor_apply_retention_last_successful_run_timestamp_seconds` stays at `0`, no marks are written, and nothing is deleted. This is a regression from **#19093** ("make index updates idempotent from horizontally scalable compactor", commit `0b2d0b070`, first released in v3.6.0). It is present in all `v3.6.x`, all `v3.7.x` (latest `v3.7.3`), and `main`. `v3.5.x` and earlier are not affected. ## Symptom Every retention cycle logs, for the table currently at the retention boundary: ``` level=error msg="failed to apply retention" table=<index_NNNNN> err="could not find entry of chunk <user>/<fp>/<from>:<through>:<checksum> to remove it" ``` `markForDelete` returns this error, the whole `RunCompaction(applyRetention=true)` aborts, `MarkPhaseFinished()` is never called, so `applyRetentionLastSuccess` is never set and the sweeper reports `no marks file found`. ## Root cause `seriesCleaner.RemoveChunk` (`pkg/storage/stores/shipper/indexshipper/boltdb/compactor/iterator.go`) recomputes a chunk's index-write entries for its full `[from, through]` via `GetChunkWriteEntries` (`pkg/storage/stores/series/index/schema.go`), which iterates **every index period the chunk overlaps**: ```go for _, bucket := range s.buckets(from, through, userID) { // one bucket per period spanned entries, _ := s.entries.GetChunkWriteEntries(bucket, ...) result = append(result, entries...) } ``` For a chunk that spans a day boundary, this yields keys for **two** day-buckets (`d<N-1>` and `d<N>`). But each per-day table only holds its own day's entries, so when processing table `index_<N>` the `d<N-1>` key is legitimately absent. `#19093` made that absence fatal: ```diff -func (s *seriesCleaner) RemoveChunk(...) error { +func (s *seriesCleaner) RemoveChunk(...) (bool, error) { indexEntries, _ := s.schema.GetChunkWriteEntries(from, through, ...) for _, indexEntry := range indexEntries { key := indexEntry.HashValue + separator + indexEntry.RangeValue - if err := s.bucket.Delete(key); err != nil { // Delete is a no-op if key absent (tolerant) - return err - } + if s.bucket.Get(key) == nil { // any absent key -> "not found" + return false, nil + } + keys = append(keys, key) } + for _, key := range keys { s.bucket.Delete(key) } - return nil + return true, nil } ``` ```diff // markForDelete, pkg/compactor/retention/retention.go -if err := indexFile.RemoveChunk(c.From, c.Through, ...); err != nil { return err } +chunkExisted, err := indexFile.RemoveChunk(c.From, c.Through, ...) +if err != nil { return err } +if !chunkExisted { + return fmt.Errorf("could not find entry of chunk %s to remove it", c.ChunkID) +} ``` Before `#19093`, `bucket.Delete` on a key that isn't in the current table was a harmless no-op, so each per-day table dropped its own entries for a spanning chunk independently and retention completed. The new "`Get` every key, fail if any is missing" logic turns the normal per-period split into a hard error. It is symmetric: processing `index_<N-1>` fails on the `d<N>` key, so both adjacent tables report `status="failure"`. Because chunks routinely stay open across midnight (see next section), the boundary table fails on essentially every retention cycle, so retention never advances. ## Chunks spanning an index-period boundary are expected by design This is not an anomaly or corrupted data — it is intrinsic to Loki's data model, which is why this regression is easy to miss but affects everyone on boltdb-shipper: - **Ingesters do not cut chunks on index-period boundaries.** Chunks are cut by age (`max_chunk_age`), size, or synchronization. `cutChunkForSynchronization` (`pkg/ingester/stream.go`) offsets each stream's sync point by its fingerprint (`(entryTimestamp + fp) % sync_period`) and only cuts above `sync_min_utilization`, so cuts are deliberately **not** wall-clock/day-aligned, and low-volume streams are not cut at all. A stream active across midnight therefore produces a chunk that spans two daily tables. - **The index model deliberately accommodates multi-period chunks.** The write path indexes a chunk in *every* period it overlaps (`GetChunkWriteEntries` → `buckets(from, through)` above), and the read path (`GetChunksForSeries`, etc.) reads across periods the same way. - **Retention itself already anticipates cross-table chunks.** `markForDelete` has a dedicated branch for `c.Through.After(tableInterval.End)` ("the chunk would also be indexed in the next table"). Both that branch and the main deletion branch now route through the strict `RemoveChunk` and hard-fail. So the correct long-term behavior is that the retention delete path must handle multi-period chunks consistently with the write/read paths (as it did before `#19093`) — the fix should not assume a chunk's entries all live in a single table. ## Reproduction 1. Configure a `boltdb-shipper` schema (`index.period: 24h`) on object storage, with compactor `retention_enabled: true`. 2. Ensure a stream stays open across a day boundary so at least one chunk spans two daily tables (normal for low-volume streams; guaranteed over time). 3. Let the retention boundary reach a day containing such a chunk. 4. On v3.6.0+: `apply_retention_last_successful_run_timestamp_seconds` stays `0`, the sweeper logs `no marks file found`, and the compactor logs `failed to apply retention … could not find entry of chunk … to remove it` on the boundary table every cycle. The same setup on v3.5.x deletes normally. ### Concrete example (schema v12) A chunk spanning `d19558` → `d19559` (open across one midnight) has these entries, one per day, in the respective tables: ``` in index_19559: fake:d19559:<seriesID>\x00<through_rel_to_d19559>\x00\x00<chunkID>\x003\x00 in index_19558: fake:d19558:<seriesID>\x00<through_rel_to_d19558>\x00\x00<chunkID>\x003\x00 ``` Both entries are present and well-formed (the index is healthy). While processing `index_19559`, `RemoveChunk` recomputes both keys and does `bucket.Get()` on each: ``` d19558 key -> nil (it lives in index_19558) => chunkExisted=false => "could not find entry of chunk" d19559 key -> found ``` ## Affected versions - Broken: **v3.6.0 → v3.7.3 (latest) and `main`** (all contain `0b2d0b070` / #19093). - Last unaffected: **v3.5.x** (`RemoveChunk(...) error`, tolerant `bucket.Delete`). - Not fixed in any release or on `main`. ## Expected behavior A chunk that spans an index-period boundary must remain removable per-table: `RemoveChunk`/`markForDelete` should only require/remove the index entries that belong to the table currently being processed (scope the recomputed entries to the table interval), and/or not treat a key that legitimately lives in an adjacent table as `chunkExisted=false`. Separately, a single table's retention error should not abort retention for all other tables. ## Not a duplicate of #20547 #20547 is the **sweep** phase timing out on marker files that already exist (`failed to process marks`). This is the **mark** phase, where no marker files are ever produced (`no marks file found`). Different phase and code path. ## Environment - Loki: reproduced on v3.7.3; regression present since v3.6.0 and on `main` - Deployment: distributed mode, object storage (S3) - Schema: `boltdb-shipper`. Only `boltdb-shipper` tables are affected; `tsdb` is not. This primarily impacts deployments still holding boltdb-shipper data within their retention window while running v3.6.0+ (i.e. mid-migration to TSDB).

signal.title: pattern tee: nil-pointer panic in distributor - TenantConfigs nil because PatternIngesterTee lacks TenantConfigs module dependency
signal.text: ## Describe the bug Distributors intermittently panic (SIGSEGV) in the pattern-ingester tee path. The panic is a nil dereference of `*runtime.TenantConfigs` inside `TeeService`. It is non-deterministic per pod: some distributor pods start, serve traffic, then crash once with `exit=2`, and usually recover on restart. ## Environment - Loki: **3.5.2** (also verified in source: v3.5.3, v3.5.5, `main`) - Mode: distributed / microservices (separate `distributor` target) - `auth_enabled: false` (single tenant `fake`) - `pattern_ingester.enabled: true` - `runtime_config` effectively empty (`{}`) ## Stack trace ``` panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x299258c] runtime.(*TenantConfigs).getOverridesForUser(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:80 runtime.(*TenantConfigs).LogPushRequestStreams(...) pkg/runtime/config.go:98 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch.func1(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:347 pattern.(*TeeService).sendBatch(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:299 pattern.(*TeeService).batchSender(...) pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:279 pattern.(*TeeService).Start.func1() pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:120 created by pattern.(*TeeService).Start pkg/pattern/tee_service.go:119 ``` ## Root cause (analysis) - `getOverridesForUser` (pkg/runtime/config.go) panics because the receiver `*TenantConfigs` (`ts.tenantCfgs`) is `nil`, not because the provider is nil. - `initPatternIngesterTee` builds the tee with `t.tenantConfigs` (pkg/loki/modules.go), but the module dependency graph does **not** list `TenantConfigs` as a dependency of `PatternIngesterTee`: ``` PatternIngesterTee: {Server, Overrides, MemberlistKV, Analytics, PatternRingClient} ``` So depending on module init order, `t.tenantConfigs` can still be `nil` when the tee is constructed. The tee stores it as-is and later dereferences it in the async `batchSender` goroutine (`tee_service.go`), with no nil guard. - This is distinct from the already-merged fixes #14665 (added `Overrides` dep, 3.3.0) and #16112 (initialize overrides for pattern tee, 3.5.0): those address the `Overrides` object, not `TenantConfigs`. - Verified the gap persists in v3.5.2, v3.5.3, v3.5.5 and `main`: `PatternIngesterTee` still omits `TenantConfigs`, and `NewTeeService` / `sendBatch` still dereference `tenantCfgs` without a nil check. ## Impact - Distributor process crash -> transient 5xx on in-flight pushes (clients retry to other distributors; effective log loss ~0), pod churn, HPA jitter. - Only the patterns write path is affected; normal ingest and queries are fine. ## Suggested fix Either (or both): 1. Add `TenantConfigs` to the `PatternIngesterTee` dependencies in `setupModuleManager` so `t.tenantConfigs` is initialized before the tee is built. 2. Add a nil guard in `TeeService` before calling `ts.tenantCfgs.LogPushRequestStreams(...)`. ## Workaround Set `pattern_ingester.enabled: false` (the tee is gated by `if !Pattern.Enabled`), which removes the tee and the panic.

signal.title: Bloom builder fails Azure uploads with "token is expired" (federated/workload identity), while chunk & compactor clients on the same identity refresh fine
signal.text: **Describe the bug** With Azure Workload Identity (`use_federated_token: true`), the **bloom-builder** fails all object-storage uploads with `InvalidAuthenticationInfo` / "Lifetime validation failed. The token is expired." once a pod is past ~1h of life. On the **same** service account, the ingester/write path (chunk flushes, incl. pods up 60+ days) and the compactor upload fine — so the federated identity itself is healthy and rotating. The bloom store uses the same client as everyone else (`NewBloomStore` → `storage.NewObjectClient(..., "bloomshipper", ...)` → `BlobStorage` with `SetCustomRefreshFunc`), and that federated-token refresh code is identical from v3.5.7 through v3.7.3 — yet only the builder fails to refresh. It looks like the deprecated `go-autorest/adal` SPT doesn't refresh reliably for the builder's infrequent/bursty access pattern (build cycles every `planning_interval`, long single tasks spanning the ~1h token lifetime). Impact: uploads never succeed → planner re-plans the same gaps every cycle → builder rebuilds blocks locally each time → the bloom shipper working dir grows unbounded and fills the backend PVC (`blocks_cache` limits don't bound builder scratch). Does [#21987 (Replace deprecated Azure SDK)](https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/21987) — moving to `WorkloadIdentityCredential`, on `main`, not yet in v3.7.3 — fix this, and which release will ship it? **To Reproduce** 1. Start Loki v3.5.7, SimpleScalable, on AKS with Azure Workload Identity: `storage.type: azure`, `use_federated_token: true`. 2. Enable blooms: `bloom_build.enabled: true`, `bloom_gateway.enabled: true`, `bloom_creation_enabled: true`, `bloom_gateway_enable_filtering: true`. 3. Let a backend pod run past ~1h and a bloom build cycle execute. 4. Watch `component=bloom-builder` logs. **Expected behavior** The bloom-builder refreshes its Azure access token (re-reading the rotated federated token file) and uploads succeed — as the chunk and compactor clients do on the same identity. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (AKS), Azure Blob storage, Azure Workload Identity - Deployment tool: helm (`loki` chart 6.42.0), SimpleScalable **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** ``` level=error caller=builder.go:519 component=bloom-builder tenant=<tenant> table=index_<N> meta=bloom/index_<N>/<tenant>/metas/<...>.json msg="failed to write meta" err="... ServiceCode=InvalidAuthenticationInfo ... AuthenticationErrorDetail: Lifetime validation failed. The token is expired. PUT https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/bloom/index_<N>/<tenant>/metas/<...>.json User-Agent: [Azure-Storage/0.14 (go1.24.8; linux)] RESPONSE Status: 401" ```

signal.title: feat(logql): Add approx_count_distinct syntax and extractor
signal.text: ## Summary First slice of experimental `approx_count_distinct` ([grafana/loki-private#2769](https://github.com/grafana/loki-private/issues/2769)). Adds LogQL syntax, AST, plan serialization, and a distinct-value extractor that hashes the counted field with xxhash64. It does **not** evaluate sketches, shard, or enable the operator. Queries parse, then fail in the engine with an unsupported-expression error. ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` New constructs: - `LabelAggregationExpr` / `labelAggOp` — generic `metricExpr` for the `op(field, log-range) by (groups)` signature that `approx_count_distinct` needs (no plans currently for additional operators, but the alternative was a specific op like ApproxCountDistinctAggExpr and that didn't fit with the other metricExpr types) - `approx_count_distinct` — the public operator; first (and currently only) `labelAggOp`. Parses to `LabelAggregationExpr` and is what users write. - `distinctValueSampleExtractor` — hashes the raw counted-field string with xxhash64 into `Sample.Value`. Lets later HLL evaluation reuse the sample iterator without creating one series per distinct value. - `CountDistinctSketchExpr` — internal shard-child expression that returns mergeable HLL sketches instead of a numeric estimate. Unused until the shard/transport PR; included now so query-plan serialization can round-trip the planned form. ## Roadmap 1. **This PR** — syntax, AST, extractor 2. Local HLL evaluation 3. Shard + protobuf sketch transport (merge-before-estimate) 4. Feature gate + result-cache bypass 5. Docs ## Review guide - Review the hand-written syntax/AST/extractor changes. - Skip `pkg/logql/syntax/syntax.y.go` (goyacc-generated). - Check the operator contract in `LabelAggregationExpr.validate` (`pkg/logql/syntax/ast.go` around line 1540) and the accepted and rejected examples in `pkg/logql/syntax/parser_test.go`. ## Risks After merging this PR, `approx_count_distinct(...) by (...)` is parseable with no feature gate. Evaluation is unimplemented, so these queries error (`unexpected expr type`) instead of returning estimates. All other existing LogQL queries are unchanged. ## Test plan - [x] `go test ./pkg/logql/log/ ./pkg/logql/syntax/`

signal.title: feat(operator): add k8s.audit.event.verb as default stream label for audit tenant
signal.text: ## What this is / why we need it The OpenShift Logging OTLP data model ([docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.5/html/configuring_logging/opentelemetry-data-model)) already maps several audit event fields to structured metadata: - `k8s.user.username` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.resource` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.namespace` - `k8s.audit.event.object_ref.name` - `k8s.audit.event.response.code` - `k8s.audit.event.user_agent` However, `verb` (the API operation: create, update, patch, delete, get, list) is **not included** in the default attribute mapping — neither as a stream label nor as structured metadata. `verb` is arguably the most important filter for audit log queries and is an ideal stream label candidate because: - **Very low cardinality**: only ~6 values (create, update, patch, delete, get, list) - **Static/long-lived**: values never change - **Most commonly used filter**: nearly every audit query filters by verb first - **Partitions search space effectively**: most audit volume is `get`/`list`, so filtering to `create`/`delete` dramatically reduces scan ## Proposal Add `k8s.audit.event.verb` as a **default stream label** for the `audit` tenant in `openshift-logging` mode. Since cardinality is ≤6, it creates at most 6 additional streams per existing stream combination — well within safe limits. Alternatively, at minimum add it as **structured metadata** so it can be used in label filter expressions without `| json` parsing. ## Context We're building an OCP audit log viewer dashboard ([PR](https://github.com/rhobs/observability-operator/pull/1134)) that filters by verb, username, resource, namespace, etc. Currently the query requires `| json` to parse every log line before filtering — making `verb` a stream label would allow the stream selector to eliminate most logs before parsing. ## References - [OpenShift Logging 6.5 OTLP data model](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.5/html/configuring_logging/opentelemetry-data-model) - [Label best practices](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/next/get-started/labels/bp-labels/) - Related: https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/21001 (stream label defaults discussion)
signal.author: sradco

signal.title: LogQL: Pretty printing json/logfmt logs
signal.text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Structured logs such as JSON or Logfmt, prevalent in most applications these days, make logs easy to query, at the expense of being difficult for humans to read. Here is one example log coming from Grafana: ``` logger=tsdb.loki endpoint=queryData pluginId=loki dsName=Loki dsUID=myuniquelokiuid uname=grafana_scheduler rule_uid=bfp7zv89ut4w0a org_id=1 fromAlert=true t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.910720711Z level=info msg="Response parsed from loki" duration=100.617µs framesLength=0 stage=parseResponse logger=ngalert.scheduler rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 version=1 fingerprint=22182789d24d049b now=2026-06-23T06:08:00Z rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.912792957Z attempt=2 max_attempts=3 next_attempt_in=1.643128315s error="the result-set has errors that can be retried: [sse.dataQueryError] failed to execute query [query]: bad_data: invalid parameter "query": 8:3: parse error: unexpected character: '|'" ``` * ❌ Human readable **msg** lost in the middle of other machine-data such as **rule_uid** and **fingerprint** * ❌ **level** lost in the middle of other machine-data * ❌ **logger** of different length misaligns the log and make it difficult to read * ❌ Noise from duplicate information such as **t**. Another example from a Python application ``` timestamp="2026-06-22 13:57:54" logger="statemonitor" level="ERROR" message="Main crashed. Goes into sleep backoff for 30 sec" thread="MainThread" user=12345, endpoint="/bar" traceback="
 File "<python-input-19>", line 4, in <module>
 lumberjack()
 ~~~~~~~~~~^^
 File "<python-input-8>", line 7, in lumberjack
 bright_side_of_life()
 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
 File "<python-input-8>", line 11, in bright_side_of_life
 return t[5]
 ~^^^
IndexError: tuple index out of range" ``` * ❌ Newlines escaped with `
` make traceback impossible to read * ❌ Attempts to restore the newlines with LogQL (`| logfmt | line_format "{{.message}} {{.traceback}}`") easily looses other KV-pairs, eg `endpoint` and `user` in the example above **Describe the solution you'd like** Helper functions in LogQL to pretty print a logfmt-formatted log, so the output after query looks as follows: ``` info tsdb.loki : Response parsed from loki. endpoint=queryData pluginId=loki dsName=Loki dsUID=myuniquelokiuid uname=grafana_scheduler rule_uid=bfp7zv89ut4w0a org_id=1 fromAlert=true duration=100.617µs framesLength=0 stage=parseResponse error ngalert.scheduler: Failed to evaluate rule. error="the result-set has errors that can be retried: [sse.dataQueryError] failed to execute query [query]: bad_data: invalid parameter "query": 8:3: parse error: unexpected character: '|'" rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 version=1 fingerprint=22182789d24d049b now=2026-06-23T06:08:00Z rule_uid=66205830-cc8a-5c16-87bc-ac6bc5b011fb org_id=1 t=2026-06-23T06:08:00.912792957Z attempt=2 max_attempts=3 next_attempt_in=1.643128315s ERROR statemonitor : Main crashed. Goes into sleep backoff for 30 sec traceback=File "<python-input-19>", line 4, in <module> lumberjack() ~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "<python-input-8>", line 7, in lumberjack bright_side_of_life() ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "<python-input-8>", line 11, in bright_side_of_life return t[5] ~^^^ IndexError: tuple index out of range thread="MainThread" user=12345, endpoint="/bar" INFO auth : Another log entry bla bla ``` * ✅ Emphasising the most relevant fields first (`message`, `logger`, `level`, `ts`) * ✅ Aligning fields that we know will always be short and first (`level` and `logger`) * ✅ Display newlines, indented to not be mixed up with other logs. * ✅ Word wrap * ✅ Present all remaining KV-pairs after the message * ✅ Truncation Suggested LogQL might look something like this: ``` | logfmt | drop ts | pretty_print (level:align, logger:align, message, error:with_key, *rest:with_key:with_newlines) ``` I have not thought in detail about the exact semantics and am happy to leave that to the experts. Things that would be of interest to control: * Alignment * Escaping newlines or not * Displaying key name or not * Handling of missing fields, silently ignoring them or showing that they are missing Defaults for good handling of `level` `lvl`, `logger`, `msg`, `message`, `ts`, `t`, `timestamp` would also be appreciated. As i believe 99% of all logs will centre around those fields. **Describe alternatives you've considered** * Concotion of `line_format` `slice`, `align_left`, `indent`, `printf` etc. - While this works okish for the left alignment. Printing "the rest" of the KV-fields becomes difficult. ` | line_format "{{(slice .builtin_levelname 0 1)}}/{{printf "%-25s" .builtin_name}} {{printf "%-10s" .msg | indent 3}} {{ range $k, $v := . }}{{ if (eq (slice $k 0 3) "ht_" ) }}{{ slice $k 3 }}={{ $v }} {{ end }}{{ end }}"` ❌ Extremely unmaintainable and ugly * Using Grafana table view exclusively to view logs ❌ Requires a lot of clicking to select the relevant fields. ❌ Selection can not be reused and shared. ❌ Only works in Grafana, not with LogCLI or when presenting the logs through other interfaces using the Loki REST API. * Change the application to print the logs in the desired order and with labels truncated to be aligned without tooling (`warning` ->`warn`) InfluxDB has such logs for example ``` ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.766046Z lvl=info msg="Welcome to InfluxDB" log_id=13WAOWTG000 version=v2.4.0 commit=de247bab08 build_date=2022-08-18T19:41:15Z log_level=info ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.766081Z lvl=warn msg="nats-port argument is deprecated and unused" log_id=13WAOWTG000 ts=2026-06-16T13:39:39.779555Z lvl=info msg="Resources opened" log_id=13WAOWTG000 service=bolt path=/var/lib/influxdb2/influxd.bolt ``` ✅ `msg` and `lvl` aligned and looks good out of the box ❌ Requires control of every application in the wild ❌ Will not work if `logger` is misaligning ❌ No story for how to deal with newlines **Additional context** https://brandur.org/logfmt#human does acknowledge that logfmt is not readable enough for humans and suggest that the presentation layer should provide additional help: > *Logfmt may be more readable than something like JSON, but it’s still difficult to scan quickly for humans.* > *In development, a log output formatter can then give the msg field special treatment by displaying it in way that a human can easily read (along with other special fields like level)*

signal.title: \u0022 unicode escaping in log messages on .NET 10
signal.text: **Describe the bug** When using `Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki` v9 with the default formatter on .NET 10, double quotes in log messages are escaped as `\u0022` in Grafana Loki instead of rendering as literal `"` characters. **To Reproduce** 1. Create an ASP.NET Core project on .NET 10 2. Add `Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki` v9 and configure with default formatter 3. Enable `UseSerilogRequestLogging` 4. Deploy to Azure App Service and check logs in Grafana Loki **Expected behavior** The logs should show without \u0022. For e.g. HTTP GET /Home/Dispatches responded 200 in 132.39 ms **Environment:** - Runtime: .NET 10 - Package: Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki 9.0.0 - Infrastructure: Azure App Service - Hosting: ASP.NET Core MVC **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Screenshot attached. **Workaround** Use `RenderedCompactJsonFormatter` from `Serilog.Formatting.Compact` as the `textFormatter` parameter on the Loki sink: ```csharp using Serilog.Formatting.Compact; cfg.WriteTo.GrafanaLoki( uri, credentials: credentials, labels: labels, propertiesAsLabels: ["level"], textFormatter: new RenderedCompactJsonFormatter()); ```

signal.title: [Helm] extraObjects: tpl re-evaluates user content, breaking Prometheus/Loki ruler templates ({{ $labels }}, {{ $value }})
signal.text: **Describe the bug** The Loki Helm chart's `extraObjects` field passes every user-provided entry through `tpl`, which re-evaluates the rendered YAML as a Helm template. Any embedded `{{ ... }}` that targets a *different* runtime (Prometheus/Loki ruler alert templates such as `{{ $labels.x }}` / `{{ $value }}`, Grafana templating, etc.) is therefore evaluated by Helm at chart-render time and fails with `undefined variable`. Concrete impact: shipping Loki ruler alert rules as a ConfigMap via `extraObjects` is impossible without manually backtick-escaping every `{{ $labels.* }}` and `{{ $value }}` in every rule. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Use Loki Helm chart `grafana/loki` (reproduced on 6.6.0; the relevant template is identical on current `main` / 7.1.0). 2. Create `values.yaml`: ```yaml extraObjects: - apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: loki-alert-rules data: rules.yaml: | groups: - name: example rules: - alert: TestAlert expr: rate({job="x"} |= "error" [5m]) > 0 annotations: summary: "Error spike on {{ $labels.cluster }}" ``` 3. Render the chart: ```bash helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.6.0 -f values.yaml ``` No Loki / Alloy instance is needed — this fails at chart render time. **Expected behavior** `helm template` renders the ConfigMap with `{{ $labels.cluster }}` preserved as a literal string, so the Loki ruler can substitute it at alert evaluation time. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes (any; bug is at `helm template` time) - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.6.0; same code in `main`) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Render error: ``` Error: template: loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml:N:M: executing "loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml" at <tpl (toYaml .) $>: error calling tpl: ... at <$labels.cluster>: undefined variable "$labels" ``` Relevant template — `production/helm/loki/templates/extra-manifests.yaml`: ```yaml {{- range $extraObjects }} --- {{- if kindIs "map" . }} {{- tpl (toYaml .) $ | nindent 0 }} # re-evaluates user content {{- else if kindIs "string" . }} {{- tpl . $ | nindent 0 }} {{- end }} {{- end }} ``` --- **Root cause** `tpl` is applied to every `extraObjects` entry so users can interpolate Helm context (e.g. `{{ .Release.Name }}`) inside their manifests. The same call also eagerly evaluates any other `{{ ... }}` it encounters, including expressions meant for a downstream runtime. Loki ruler templating is the most common collision because the ruler ConfigMap pattern is widely used. **Current workaround** Backtick-escape each `{{ ... }}` so Helm emits a literal: ```yaml summary: "Error spike on {{ `{{ $labels.cluster }}` }}" ``` Works but is intrusive — a rule with 3 annotations needs 3 escapes each, and every new rule needs the same treatment. Copy-pasting rules from an existing Prometheus deployment doesn't just work. **Proposed fix** Add an additive, non-breaking values key `extraObjectsNoTpl` that mirrors `extraObjects` but skips `tpl`: ```yaml # values.yaml # Extra Kubernetes manifests appended to the release, NOT processed through # `tpl`. Use this for content containing expressions that must reach the # runtime as-is — e.g. Prometheus / Loki ruler alert templates # ({{ $labels.x }}, {{ $value }}). For content that needs Helm variable # interpolation, use `extraObjects` instead. extraObjectsNoTpl: [] ``` ```yaml # templates/extra-manifests.yaml — additional block {{- range .Values.extraObjectsNoTpl }} --- {{- if kindIs "map" . }} {{- toYaml . | nindent 0 }} {{- else if kindIs "string" . }} {{- . | nindent 0 }} {{- end }} {{- end }} ``` API rule: "tpl needed → `extraObjects`; raw → `extraObjectsNoTpl`". Existing `extraObjects` behavior unchanged. **Offer to send PR** Happy to open a PR implementing `extraObjectsNoTpl` (template + `values.yaml` + `values.schema.json` + `ci/` test + README) if maintainers are open to this shape. If a different API is preferred (per-entry flag, opt-out on `extraObjects`, etc.), please advise before I cut the PR. **Related** #11796 — different `extraObjects` rendering issue (uses `include`). This report specifically covers the runtime-template-variable collision via `tpl`.

signal.title: Compactor delete-request-store initialization fails independently of the main S3 object-store client
signal.text: ## Problem In Loki 3.6.11, the main object-store path and the compactor delete-request-store path are initialized separately. In my production setup with an Amazon S3 Express One Zone directory bucket, the main storage client can operate, but the compactor can still fail during delete-request-store initialization when retention is enabled. The failure I see is: ```text failed to init delete store: Get "https://<bucket>.s3express-<zone>.<region>.amazonaws.com/?session=": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ``` ## The two client-creation paths ### 1) Main object/data/index client Loki creates the main object clients here: - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1670-1681` builds the per-period object clients with `storage.NewObjectClient(periodConfig.ObjectType, "compactor", ...)` - `pkg/storage/factory.go:658-709` routes S3 backends to `aws.NewS3ObjectClient(...)` - `pkg/storage/chunk/client/aws/s3_storage_client.go:176-255` builds the AWS S3 client and applies `http_config.ca_file` to the HTTP transport ### 2) Compactor delete-request-store client The delete-store client is created separately here: - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1684-1690` builds `storage.NewObjectClient(deleteStore, "delete-store", ...)` - `pkg/loki/modules.go:1696-1700` passes that client into the compactor - `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:212-219` immediately initializes delete handling when `retention_enabled` is true - `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:315-336` wires the delete-request store into the deletion manager ## Why this matters The compactor startup path touches the delete-request-store immediately when retention is enabled, so any TLS / trust-store mismatch on that path prevents the backend from starting even though the main object-store path is a separate client and may otherwise behave differently at runtime. In practice this is painful for S3 Express because the failure happens during the `CreateSession`/session bootstrap path for the directory bucket, and the pod can look like it is failing only at startup rather than during ordinary reads/writes. ## Expected behavior The delete-request-store client should inherit the same S3 TLS trust configuration as the main object-store client, or Loki should expose a clear, documented way to configure the CA bundle for that path as well. ## Suggested fix Please review whether the delete-request-store initialization path is missing parity with the main object-store path for custom TLS trust / CA bundle handling, especially for S3 Express directory buckets.

signal.title: feat(logql): Add approx_count_distinct aggregation
signal.text: ## Summary - Adds experimental LogQL `approx_count_distinct` to approximate distinct values of a label or extracted field without creating one series per distinct value. - Instant queries only; each output group holds one HyperLogLog sketch (precision 14, ~16 KiB dense, ~0.81% nominal RSE). - Supports index sharding when `approx_count_distinct` is listed in `shard_aggregations`; shards return mergeable sketches and the frontend merges before estimating. - Requires `frontend.encoding: protobuf` (JSON internal transport is rejected). Result caching is disabled for these queries. ### Syntax ```logql approx_count_distinct( <counted field>, <log expression> [<duration>] ) by (<grouping fields>) ``` Example: ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` `by (...)` is required. `unwrap`, ungrouped forms, `without`, and prefix grouping are not supported. The counted field must not appear in `by (...)`. ### Enablement ```yaml limits_config: shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct] frontend: encoding: protobuf ``` Off by default until `approx_count_distinct` is added to `shard_aggregations`. Grafana Cloud can follow the existing `approx_topk` enablement pattern in `ksonnet/lib/loki-cloud-mixin/limits.libsonnet`. ### Implementation notes - Public AST: `LabelAggregationExpr`; shard children use internal `CountDistinctSketchExpr` (merge-before-estimate). - Distinct-value extractor hashes the raw string with xxhash64 into `Sample.Value` via `Float64frombits`; evaluator inserts with `InsertHash`. - Range splitting is rejected as unsafe for HLL estimates; outer non-HLL aggregations over this op remain non-shardable. - Output cardinality is bounded by grouping labels / `max_query_series`, not by distinct counted values. Peak sketch memory scales with group count (~16 KiB dense per group) and is not capped by `max_query_series` alone. ## Test plan - [ ] `go test ./pkg/logql/ ./pkg/logql/syntax/ ./pkg/logql/log/ ./pkg/querier/queryrange/ ./pkg/logproto/ ./pkg/chunkenc/` - [ ] Instant query returns per-group estimates; missing/empty counted fields are skipped - [ ] With `shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct]`, shard mapper rewrites to merge-before-estimate and merged estimates match local evaluation - [ ] Without the gate / without protobuf encoding, queries are rejected - [ ] Range queries are rejected - [ ] Staging enablement before broader rollout

signal.title: fix(indexgateway): Cap client-side in-flight requests to avoid retry amplification
signal.text: Fixes #24051 ## What this does `poolDo` had no bound on concurrent in-flight requests to the index gateway pool. With `maxRetries = -1` (used by 6 of the 7 call sites), a client under load would serially walk every address in the pool on failure, each attempt bounded by that gateway's own admission-control queue timeout (from #23932). When every replica is shedding load, this amplifies load at exactly the moment the pool is most overloaded, instead of failing fast. ## The fix Adds a configurable client-side cap on in-flight requests (`-index-gateway-client.max-in-flight-requests`, default 2048, 0 = unlimited to match the convention used elsewhere in this file). The check runs at the very start of `poolDo`, before any tenant lookup or address resolution — once at capacity, requests are rejected immediately with a distinct error instead of retrying across the whole pool. Tracked via a new `loki_index_gateway_request_rejected_total` counter so operators can see this happening rather than it being silent. One deliberate tradeoff: the cap check is check-then-act, not a single atomic compare-and-swap, so under concurrency the actual in-flight count can briefly exceed the configured cap by a small margin. Noted in a code comment — this is acceptable for a soft limit meant to prevent amplification storms, not a hard resource cap. ## Testing Added four tests covering: rejection at cap (verified by confirming the capacity error returns before any tenant/address lookup would even be attempted), the in-flight counter decrementing after both success and failure paths (proving the `defer` fires on every exit), and `MaxInFlightRequests = 0` correctly disabling the check. Happy to adjust the default cap value or error message if you'd prefer something different.

signal.title: feat(logcli): return errors from library and handle fatal in CLI
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: The `logcli` package calls `log.Fatal` in ~20 places, which terminates the process from inside library code. That makes the package unusable as a library: an embedding application gets no chance to retry, fall back, or clean up, because the process is already gone. This PR changes those functions to return errors instead, and moves the fatal handling up into the CLI layer (`cmd/logcli/main.go`), so the `logcli` binary keeps its current behavior. **What changed**: *Signature changes* — `error` added as the last return value: | Package | Functions | | --- | --- | | `pkg/logcli/detected` | `(*FieldsQuery).Do` | | `pkg/logcli/index` | `(*StatsQuery).DoStats`, `(*StatsQuery).Stats`, `GetVolume`, `GetVolumeRange` | | `pkg/logcli/labelquery` | `(*LabelQuery).DoLabels`, `(*LabelQuery).ListLabels` | | `pkg/logcli/seriesquery` | `(*SeriesQuery).DoSeries`, `(*SeriesQuery).GetSeries` | | `pkg/logcli/query` | `(*Query).DoQuery`, `(*Query).DoQueryParallel`, `(*Query).TailQuery` | | `pkg/logcli/print` | `(*QueryResultPrinter).PrintResult` | | `pkg/logcli/output` | `LogOutput.FormatAndPrintln` (interface) and its three implementations | Seven unexported helpers (`do`, `getVolume`, `printStream`, `printMatrix`, `printVector`, `printScalar`, `createPartFile`) were updated to match. *CLI layer* — `cmd/logcli/main.go` now handles each returned error with `log.Fatalf`, so the binary's output and exit codes stay the same as before, except where noted below. *Tests* — 11 new tests covering error propagation and success paths for the entry points above, in `detected`, `index`, `labelquery`, `seriesquery`, `output`, and `query`. **Intentional behavior changes**: These are not pure refactoring, so I'm calling them out explicitly: 1. **Tail failures now exit non-zero.** When reading the tail stream fails, or reconnection attempts are exhausted, `TailQuery` previously logged the error and returned, so `logcli tail` exited 0 and hid the failure from scripts and supervisors. It now returns the error, and the CLI exits 1. 2. **`TailQuery` no longer calls `os.Exit(0)` from its signal handler.** On SIGINT/SIGTERM it cancels an internal context, so the read loop returns normally and `TailQuery` returns `nil`. The binary still exits 0, but the caller's deferred cleanup now runs. This is required for the package to work as a library — `os.Exit` in library code kills the host process. 3. **`output.LogOutput` is a breaking interface change.** `FormatAndPrintln` now returns `error`, so any out-of-tree implementation needs updating. **Out of scope / follow-up**: An earlier revision of this PR also reworked the tail connection lifecycle (cancellation plumbing, WebSocket cleanup, context-aware reconnection, and a `LiveTailQueryConnContext` method on the client). As @bboreham and @chaudum pointed out, that is a separate concern, so I've removed it here. I'll open a follow-up PR with those changes once this one lands. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #18754 **Special notes for your reviewer**: **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. signal.title: fix: Add meaningful chunk fetch loss metrics
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: `Fetcher.FetchChunks` logs an object store error and then returns a nil error. The query gets fewer log lines, HTTP 200, and no signal. We do not measure how often this occurs yet. This PR adds `loki_chunk_fetcher_failures_total{source,reason}`. It counts each lost chunk and the reason for the loss. This PR yet doesn't change the end-user behavior yet. It only addresses the propagation of metrics downstream. Also, a cache decode failure no longer reports `msg="failed downloading chunks"`, because that call never used storage. Currently, the counter over-reports. Query iterators fetch one batch ahead and do not join that batch on close, so a query that stops early still counts that batch. Most of that is `reason=canceled`. Use `reason!~"canceled|deadline"` for the data loss signal. Subsequent PRs to extend these will follow. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #<issue number> **Special notes for your reviewer**: **Checklist** - [ ] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [ ] Tests updated - [ ] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. [Example PR](https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/10840/commits/0d4416a4b03739583349934b96f272fb4f685d15)

signal.title: feat: Collapse max request body size and decompressed size
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: This commit collapses the max-recv-msg-size, which measures the size of the HTTP request body, and the max decompressed size (i.e. if the request has been Gzip or Snappy compressed) into a single flag. As far as Loki is concerned, we only care about the maximum size of the actual logproto that is parsed out of the request after any decompression. It doesn't make sense to have two different flags for this with the same value. You will notice that in http.go we pass the same flag twice to push.ParseRequest. This is temporary, and the only reason for it is to make the diff smaller and easier to review. signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: Sets sort-schema as the sort-schema for new objects. The PR takes the opportunity for code simplification. * Adds sort-schema as a flag * Always defaults to `label:service_name` for every tenant if nothing else is set. * Removes configuration for "legacy" sort schemas (stream ASC and timestamp DESC) since sort-schemas are required for compaction anyway.

signal.title: chore: Wire up a separate logsobj builder config
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: Wires up a separate configuration for logsobj vs indexobj so we don't need to use the same for both. From experience, these are similar but we use smaller page sizes on index objects I updated the defaults against the latest recommendations. This ends up wiring all the way through multiple layers so there a lot of small changes in many files.
signal.author: benclive

signal.title: feat(dataobj): Enable lazy downloading of pages in batches when reading dataobj
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: This PR introduces the behaviour implied by the Row Downloader comments. Previously there was no target size and each request under a non-prefetched reader would fetch very few pages. This changes enables a batch of pages to be fetched at once, up to the requested size, in order to balance memory usage versus object storage requests. I didn't expose this as a config param because I think a sensible default is best. I don't think this is easy to tune without knowing the internals of the system (how big are sections when compressed, which cloud provider etc.). If different target sizes are required, it can be exposed as a parameter later.
signal.author: benclive

signal.title: chore: Run index merge phase multiple times per log merge phase
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: This runs 3x index compactions for every log merge done by the compactor. Each merge reduces Runs by K, but each log merge increases it again by K * (The K can be different for index & log merge, but in reality they are in the same ballpark) This means index-compaction doesn't make progress if it flip-flops 1-1. This PR improves that behaviour by running 3x index merges to reduce index Runs by K^3 per each log-merge. This is enough to converge the index files to a single Run in most environments.

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/23439) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go (go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric)</summary> ### [`v1.45.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.45.0): /v0.67.0/v0.21.0/v0.0.18 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/compare/v1.44.0...v1.45.0) ##### Overview ##### Added - Add experimental observability metrics to `BatchProcessor` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​7124](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7124)) - Add the experimental `WithUnsafeAttributes` no-copy attribute option to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x` for future performance improvements. This API is a work in progress. ([#​8251](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8251)) - Add `Map` and `MapValue` functions for the new `MAP` attribute type in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8445](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8445)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/zipkin`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Apply `AttributeValueLengthLimit` recursively to values contained in `attribute.MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`. ([#​8454](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8454)) - Remove duplicate keys from `attribute.MAP` values in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in span, event, link, and instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in measurement and instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Extend `WithAllowKeyDuplication` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` to disable duplicate-key removal in `attribute.MAP` values for instrumentation scope attributes. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Add the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.42.0` package. The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.42.0` version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.42.0/MIGRATION.md) for information on how to upgrade from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.41.0`. ([#​8484](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8484)) - Add `WithoutPanicRecording` as a `TracerProviderOption` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` to disable exception event recording for panics. ([#​8532](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8532)) - Add the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.43.0` package. The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.43.0` version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.43.0/MIGRATION.md) for information on how to upgrade from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.42.0`. ([#​8628](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8628)) ##### Changed - `HistogramReservoir` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar` now uses a time-unbiased sampling algorithm for exemplars. ([#​8306](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8306)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** Use `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.Value` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.KeyValue` for log bodies and attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log/logtest`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log/logtest`. ([#​8490](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8490)) - Encode log bodies and attributes as `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.Value` JSON in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/stdout/stdoutlog`. ([#​8490](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8490)) - Improve the performance of hashing `BOOLSLICE`, `INT64SLICE`, `FLOAT64SLICE`, and `STRINGSLICE` attribute values by avoiding reflection for short slices in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8511](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8511)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** `WithEndpointURL` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp` no longer appends the default signal path when an endpoint URL has no path, making the behavior consistent with `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp` and with setting the endpoint through `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`. If the URL has no path component, the root path (`/`) is used. Use `WithEndpointURL(url.JoinPath(endpoint, "/v1/metrics"))` to preserve the previous behavior. ([#​8538](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8538)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** `WithEndpointURL` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp` no longer appends the default signal path when an endpoint URL has no path, making the behavior consistent with `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp` and with setting the endpoint through `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`. If the URL has no path component, the root path (`/`) is used. Use `WithEndpointURL(url.JoinPath(endpoint, "/v1/traces"))` to preserve the previous behavior. ([#​8538](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8538)) ##### Deprecated - Deprecate `WithExportBufferSize` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. The option remains available for source compatibility but no longer affects behavior; `BatchProcessor` no longer maintains a separate export-request buffer. ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8620)) ##### Removed - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** Remove `Kind`, `Value`, `KeyValue`, their constructors, and attribute conversion helpers from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`. ([#​8490](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8490)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** Remove the `AttributeValueLengthLimit` and `AttributeCountLimit` fields from `RecordFactory` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log/logtest`; records produced by the factory now keep attribute limits disabled so test code can append exact attributes. ([#​8556](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8556)) ##### Fixed - Apply TLS certificates configured through environment variables to gRPC connections in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc`. - Prevent panics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/bridge/opentracing` when OpenTracing baggage is propagated concurrently with `Span.SetBaggageItem`. - Fix an off-by-one error in `FixedSizeReservoir` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar` that prevented the first exemplar from being sampled after the reservoir was filled. ([#​8309](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8309)) - Interpret HTTP `Retry-After` header values as seconds instead of nanoseconds when retrying OTLP HTTP exports in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp`. ([#​8383](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8383)) - Fix a memory leak in the `Reservoir` implementation in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar`, where storing the full `context.Context` pinned large objects such as gRPC transport buffers. ([#​8389](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8389)) - Prevent a non-empty attribute set whose computed hash is zero from collapsing to an empty set in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8402](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8402)) - Fix histogram data point reuse in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` aggregation to avoid leaking stale sum, minimum, and maximum values when they are disabled in subsequent collections. ([#​8403](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8403)) - Avoid preallocating scope attributes when they are disabled in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus`. ([#​8404](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8404)) - Support HTTP-date values in the HTTP `Retry-After` header when retrying OTLP HTTP exports in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp`. ([#​8417](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8417)) - Reduce histogram heap allocations by reusing `BucketCounts` and `Exemplars` slices across `Collect` cycles in the cumulative histogram aggregation in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​8428](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8428)) - Fix `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/stdout/stdouttrace` self-observability to record `error.type` on the operation-duration histogram when the `exportedSpans` metric is disabled. ([#​8432](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8432)) - Stop including trace exporter endpoint configuration in internal logs from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/zipkin`. ([#​8438](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8438)) - Fix invalid error formatting for out-of-range JSON code values in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes`. ([#​8497](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8497)) - Clarify in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` that `Logger.Enabled` should be checked for every log emission because its result may change over time. ([#​8565](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8565)) - Preserve user-provided exception attributes while independently deriving missing exception message and type attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​8566](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8566)) - Make `WithAttributeCountLimit(0)` and `OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT=0` discard all log record attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​8570](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8570)) - Clarify that the `Record` methods of `Float64Histogram` and `Int64Histogram` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric` expect non-negative values. ([#​8574](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8574)) - Clarify in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` that `LoggerProvider` implementations should retain an empty `Logger` name instead of replacing it with a default. ([#​8587](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8587)) - Ensure that the built-in processors in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` call exporter `ForceFlush` during `Shutdown`. ([#​8599](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8599)) - Prevent panics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/bridge/opentracing` when OpenTracing baggage is propagated concurrently with `Span.SetBaggageItem`. ([GHSA-42cj-99w8-cp2p](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-42cj-99w8-cp2p)) - Prevent processor operations in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` from overlapping with processor shutdown or running after `LoggerProvider` shutdown. ([#​8608](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8608)) - Prevent `BatchProcessor` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` from busy-spinning under exporter backpressure and serialize dequeue, export, force-flush, and shutdown work in one worker. ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8620)) - Make `BatchProcessor` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` return errors encountered while draining records during `ForceFlush` and `Shutdown`, while continuing to attempt later batches as long as the request context remains valid. ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8620)) - Keep the default `BatchProcessor` maximum export batch size in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` at or below the configured maximum queue size. ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8620)) ##### What's Changed - fix(semconv): share metric option pools by [@​macayu17](https://redirect.github.com/macayu17) in [#​8371](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8371) - This API is a work in progress. ([#​8251](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8251)) - Add `Map` and `MapValue` functions for the new `MAP` attribute type in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Support `MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/zipkin`. ([#​8453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8453)) - Apply `AttributeValueLengthLimit` recursively to values contained in `attribute.MAP` attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`. ([#​8454](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8454)) - Remove duplicate keys from `attribute.MAP` values in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in span, event, link, and instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Remove duplicate keys by default from `attribute.MAP` values in measurement and instrumentation scope attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` using last-value-wins semantics. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Extend `WithAllowKeyDuplication` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` to disable duplicate-key removal in `attribute.MAP` values for instrumentation scope attributes. ([#​8471](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8471)) - Add the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.42.0` package. The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.42.0` version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.42.0/MIGRATION.md) for information on how to upgrade from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.41.0`. ([#​8484](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8484)) - Add `WithoutPanicRecording` as a `TracerProviderOption` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` to disable exception event recording for panics. ([#​8532](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8532)) - Add the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.43.0` package. The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.43.0` version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.43.0/MIGRATION.md) for information on how to upgrade from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.42.0`. ([#​8628](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8628)) ##### Changed - `HistogramReservoir` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar` now uses a time-unbiased sampling algorithm for exemplars. ([#​8306](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8306)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** Use `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.Value` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.KeyValue` for log bodies and attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log/logtest`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log/logtest`. ([#​8490](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8490)) - Encode log bodies and attributes as `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.Value` JSON in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/stdout/stdoutlog`. ([#​8490](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8490)) - Improve the performance of hashing `BOOLSLICE`, `INT64SLICE`, `FLOAT64SLICE`, and `STRINGSLICE` attribute values by avoiding reflection for short slices in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8511](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8511)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** `WithEndpointURL` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp` no longer appends the default signal path when an endpoint URL has no path, making the behavior consistent with `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp` and with setting the endpoint through `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`. If the URL has no path component, the root path (`/`) is used. Use `WithEndpointURL(url.JoinPath(endpoint, "/v1/metrics"))` to preserve the previous behavior. ([#​8538](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8538)) - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** `WithEndpointURL` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp` no longer appends the default signal path when an endpoint URL has no path, making the behavior consistent with `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp` and with setting the endpoint through `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`. If the URL has no path component, the root path (`/`) is used. Use `WithEndpointURL(url.JoinPath(endpoint, "/v1/traces"))` to preserve the previous behavior. ([#​8538](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8538)) ##### Deprecated - Deprecate `WithExportBufferSize` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8620)) ##### Removed - ⚠️ **Breaking Change:** Remove `Kind`, `Value`, `KeyValue`, their constructors, and attribute conversion helpers from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`.
